# Progressive source-grounded building product

The active specification is [PRODUCT_SPEC.md](PRODUCT_SPEC.md). It supersedes older exclusions of persistence, background jobs and review loops. Preserve the current configurable reconstruction model; Hydrogen was not adopted. No general-purpose agent runtime, database, external rendering service or new dependencies.

## Reviewed checkpoints and ownership

1. Frontend ports the existing concept renderer selectively from the read-only concept worktree. Keep current inspection fixes. Add source/proposal picking and disclosure, footprint containment/fallback, a keyed decoration ledger, offscreen preparation and atomic viewer swaps. Preserve camera, target, modes, floor, separation, cutaway, assumptions and surviving selections. Never mutate reasoning/export data.
2. Root owns filesystem building bundles, content identity, immutable revisions, CAS publication, stable object IDs and frozen source frames. Store original bytes/pages, descriptions/native records, reasoning, IFC, scene, mappings, assumptions, findings and pipeline metadata. Restore existing artifact IDs and exact descriptions. New server-owned IDs survive insertion/reordering; deleted IDs are tombstoned.
3. Backend owns shared reasoning and native IFC extraction: complete semantic identity catalog including geometry-less objects, properties/quantities/units, supplied relationships, explicitly calculated summaries, missing/coverage records and original references. Drawings keep fallible interpretations plus original visual evidence; generated IFC never becomes native factual evidence.
4. Root owns the lightweight background runner/API; backend owns model review/patch hooks and actual-IFC overlay images. Publish initial usable preview before review, accept only targeted source-supported patches, reopen candidate geometry, audit disappeared/unresolved objects and review regressions. Preserve best revision on failure, stop, stale result, no progress or budget exhaustion.
5. Backend owns reviewed QA: pinned revision, relevant structured/source context, existing sufficiency gate, internal draft, deterministic references/units/calculations, one four-way Decisions support judgment, one meaningful repair and second review if necessary. No published unreviewed claim or repeated paraphrase-until-approval. Root integrates asynchronous progress and final highlight revalidation; frontend keeps exploration usable.
6. Root integrates all acceptance flows; independent reviewer checks code and directly uses browser/original overlays. Separate live inference from fixtures and report source-fidelity failures without hiding earlier usable artifacts.

Planner and independent reviewer approved checkpoint 1 and the full plan after one clarification round. Reviewers do not implement their own reviewed paths. Root owns contracts/commits. Frontend owns static files and focused browser tests; backend owns reasoning, review schemas, provider adapters, QA service and focused tests. Existing unrelated worktrees/untracked files remain untouched.

## Shared contracts

- `Document` pins original `source_bytes`, pages, `description`, JSON `reasoning`, building/revision identifiers, monotonic revision number, identity/frame registries and transient question context. `snapshot()` deep-copies interpretation/context and shares immutable source bytes/pages.
- `Scene` retains old fields and adds optional building/revision/parent identifiers, monotonic `revision_number`, and `review_status`. UUID identifiers are never ordered. Viewer candidates capture the current base; stale commits fail. Polling may skip intermediate revisions, so a new scene need not have the displayed revision as its immediate parent.
- All description records gain optional server-managed `persistent_id`. New initial/inserted IDs are assigned by code, never trusted from the model. Existing imported IDs survive migration; immutable target IDs and tombstones prevent reassignment. New artifacts persist identities/frames with a versioned manifest; old artifacts remain readable.
- Ordinary bbox edits do not alter stored floor transforms. Supported orientation/calibration changes require explicit source-backed transform updates. Page-relative scale and cross-page schematic status remain intact.
- `review_reconstruction(document, description, scene, previous_description=None, previous_scene=None, previous_review=None)` examines original full pages/regions plus actual reopened-IFC overlays. Findings identify stable IDs/source, discrepancy, category, evidence, action and uncertainty.
- `patch_reconstruction(document, description, scene, review)` returns a base-revision-bound list of typed add/replace/remove record operations with source evidence and reasons; never executable code. Floor replacement cannot rewrite nested collections. Candidate review and local disappearance/source checks must pass before CAS publication.
- `review_answer(document, question, draft, gate, crop, validation=...)` returns supported/contradicted/unsupported/unclear. `revise_answer(...)` must add actual evidence, repair a bound calculation/citation or narrow/remove unsupported claims. Same-assertion rephrasing is not progress. A model reviewer corroborates, never certifies accuracy.
- Native reasoning may reference storeys/openings/relationships absent from render meshes. Citation validation uses faithful reasoning records; highlighting uses conservative source associations. Complete object catalog, selected context coverage, property coverage and geometry availability are separate states. Calculations resolve source values and units in code; missing inputs never become a complete total.

## Explicit operating budgets

Communicated as design choices, not external limits: background reconstruction call 300 seconds / 65,536 output tokens, whole job 900 seconds, at most two targeted patch attempts; reconstruction review 120 seconds / 16,384 tokens. QA total 180 seconds, existing 45-second per-call ceiling clamped to remaining time, at most two post-draft reviews and one meaningful correction, retaining one targeted unclear inspection. Configuration can change these limits explicitly; exhaustion means processing stopped, not source insufficiency. No new floor/room/vertex/feature caps. Existing upload/IFC safeguards remain unless separately justified.

## Acceptance audit

Every requirement in PRODUCT_SPEC remains in scope. Track live versus fixture evidence for: concept integration and safe proposals; restart/repeat-upload reopening without inference; stable ID/coordinate insertion/reorder; preview during review; source-backed correction; rejected regression; atomic no-camera-reset replacement and retained controls; stale job/patch/QA handling; source/assumption portability; genuine IFC JSON/count/property/relationship/geometry coverage including geometry-less objects and incomplete totals; drawing QA citations/highlights; actual-height refusal; meaningful post-draft repair/uncertainty; before/after original overlays for both unchanged examples; comparative QA outcomes, usage and latency; real browser performance and software limitations; focused commits and reproducible saved-building demo.

Architecture or mocked success alone is not completion. Preserve known fidelity limitations and failed live experiments. Finish only after integrated verification and no unreported blocking review findings.
# Source-first contract

Implemented checkpoint, 2026-11-14. This extends `CONTRACT.md`, `PRODUCT_PLAN.md` and the reviewed `SOURCE_FIRST_PLAN.md`; final acceptance is tracked separately in `SOURCE_FIRST_VERIFICATION.md`. JSON uses snake_case. The configurable reconstruction default remains `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`; Gemini remains the final-demo provider, with explicit `AI_PROVIDER=openai` compatibility and no automatic failover.

## Sources, identities and revisions

The building ID remains the SHA-256 identity of its initial upload. Each source has its own SHA-256 `source_id`, independent of filename. Original bytes and normalized pages are preserved in filesystem resources; filenames can be aliases. A revision pins its source membership, source-local page mappings, interpretation, identity/frame registries, user inputs and available geometry. A building retains its identity when sources are appended.

Each public page has `page`, `source_id`, `source_page`, `source_filename`, `width`, `height` and `image_url`. `page` is the append-only building page number; `source_page` is the page/layout within that file. Regions use normalized decimal fractions from 0 to 1 in the original displayed page. Pixels, percentages and 0–1000 integer coordinates are rejected, not silently divided. Referenced `page`, `source_id` and `source_page` must agree. Existing page-only references resolve against their pinned revision.

Resources store successful independent per-source interpretations. A cache merge remaps every local page reference into the selected building and assigns building-specific stable IDs. Adding B does not re-extract A. Reopening, renamed byte-identical uploads, orbiting and mode switching do not invoke inference. Failed/interrupted extraction requires explicit retry. Ordinary questions are not answer-cached. Complete retained legacy descriptions are reused; missing new cache fields do not themselves require another inference call.

Possible repeated floor views are conservative: normalized word-contained labels (for example `Erdgeschoss` and `Grundriss Erdgeschoss`) or the same explicitly supported order retain the incoming diagram as a source-linked unresolved alternate view and preserve its semantic observations. This avoids silently creating another storey; it does not establish equivalence or fuse their geometry. Uncertain alignment and differing measurements remain attributed.

**Grouping limitation:** genuine native IFC must be opened as a separate building. Grouping it with another source/native IFC is rejected before publishing a mixed bundle. This is a lean implementation limitation: the current combined drawing pipeline does not supply a complete mixed native-record catalog. Drawing-derived IFC retains drawing authority and can contribute recoverable embedded original sources. Native IFC still uses its complete supplied semantic catalog, including geometry-less records; generated IFC never becomes factual native evidence.

## Public document and job state

Public documents retain prior fields and add `sources`, `interpretation_status`, `geometry_status` and `geometry_revision_id`. `interpretation_status` is `pending`, `partial` or `complete`. Geometry is `not_requested`, `available` or `stale`. `has_scene` means a saved scene exists, not that every source feature has geometry or the model is accurate. After source changes, a retained scene can belong to `geometry_revision_id` rather than the current interpretation revision; it must not be presented as regenerated geometry.

Job kinds are `extraction`, `reconstruction`, `question` and `refinement`. Statuses are `queued`, `running`, `complete`, `needs_attention`, `failed`, `budget_exhausted`, `stopped` and `interrupted`. Jobs include identity, building/base/current revision, phase, message, timestamps, issues and attempts; usage and operation-specific results appear when available. Failure fields include `error_stage`, `error_category`, `diagnostic_id`, safe `diagnostic_message` and `has_previous_model`. A failure with no usable model says sources were saved and no usable model was generated. Valid saved interpretation survives geometry failure.

Returned structured responses may be retained privately for replay; raw provider requests, credentials and exception bodies are not logged or exposed. Stop prevents late publication; an in-flight call may finish. Revision compare-and-swap, guarded publication and per-source merging prevent a late extraction/geometry result from dropping appended sources or user inputs. Restart marks unfinished jobs interrupted while preserving sources and accepted revisions.

## HTTP endpoints

| Method and path | Request / result |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/documents` | Multipart legacy `file` and/or repeated `files`. Returns public document plus `is_new_upload`, `added_source_ids`, `extraction_jobs`. New uncached drawing sources automatically queue interpretation; no automatic 3D. |
| `POST /api/buildings/{id}/sources` | Same multipart fields, append to selected building; same result shape. |
| `GET /api/buildings` | `{buildings:[public_document]}`. |
| `GET /api/buildings/{id}` | Public document plus persisted `jobs`, newest first. |
| `POST /api/buildings/{id}/extraction` | `{source_ids?:[id], retry:true}`; HTTP 202 `{jobs:[job]}`. Successful existing interpretation is reused; failed/interrupted sources can retry. |
| `POST /api/buildings/{id}/reconstruction` | `{base_revision_id?, mode:"refine"|"reconstruct"}`; HTTP 202 job. Explicit geometry generation/refinement. |
| `GET /api/jobs/{id}` | Persisted job and final `answer` for completed questions. |
| `POST /api/jobs/{id}/stop` | Updated stop status. |
| `GET /api/buildings/{id}/revisions/{revision}/pages/{page}` | Exact revision-pinned normalized PNG. A page added later is unavailable in an older revision. |
| `GET /api/documents/{id}/pages/{page}` | Compatibility current-page PNG route. |
| `GET /api/buildings/{id}/sources/{source_id}/original` | Preserved original bytes as attachment; no raw SVG is embedded in the browser. |
| `GET /api/buildings/{id}/revisions/{revision}/evidence/{object_id}` | Original native IFC record and coverage for the pinned revision; rejects drawing-derived factual shortcuts. |
| `GET /api/documents/{id}/scene` | Saved scene; 404 if none. |
| `POST /api/documents/{id}/scene` | Compatibility explicit synchronous generation with `{page:1}`; uses the job workflow and reuses an existing scene. The page argument does not restrict whole-building generation. |
| `GET /api/documents/{id}/model.ifc` | Saved IFC download; 404 before generation. |
| `GET /api/buildings/{id}/conversation` | `{conversation_id:id,messages:[...]}`. |
| `POST /api/questions` | `AskRequest`; HTTP 202 revision-pinned question job. |
| `POST /api/ask` | Compatibility synchronous `AskRequest` → final `Answer`; also persists turns. |
| `GET /api/buildings/{id}/assumptions` | `{building_id,revision_id,rows,editable_properties}`. |
| `POST /api/buildings/{id}/refinements` | Batch request below; HTTP 202 job. |

Expanded failed-job details show only the existing sanitized `diagnostic_message`, escaped as text; raw provider errors and requests are never displayed. Operational failures are not source-insufficiency judgments. Stale revision submissions return 409. Unknown source references and invalid typed edits are rejected. `/api/health` reports provider/model configuration and existing per-file limits, not successful provider access.

## Shared interpretation and optional geometry

`BuildingDescription` remains the shared representation: floors, semantic records, observations, unresolved views and optional geometry. Empty geometric arrays do not make the original evidence unavailable. Sections/elevations can supply source-linked observations and dimensions without becoming floors. Reasoning objects and floor context derive from saved interpretation even when no scene exists.

`extract_interpretation(document, include_geometry=False)` requests source-linked semantics/observations without exhaustive geometry tracing. Each successful result is validated and saved before any generator call. QA can inspect original pages before extraction completes and after reconstruction fails; missing JSON records never establish absent source features.

Explicit generation reuses saved interpretation and requests missing geometry/registration/stair relationships through `enrich_geometry(document) -> DescriptionPatch`. Application validation remains collection-specific and strict. Gemini's wire encodes each complete patch record as a JSON string (or null for removal): the combined typed union was rejected by the endpoint, while generic objects produced empty records. Decoded record objects still pass local typed `DescriptionPatch` validation. OpenAI retains its typed transport. This adaptation does not permit executable code, unknown fields, arbitrary identity changes or invented user provenance. See the verification report for controlled probes and actual live outcomes.

Typed patches preserve existing persistent IDs and require original source evidence. A floor metadata replacement cannot execute implicit nested edits. Its nested copies must preserve base/current ID order and length and exactly match base/current records or separately declared same-floor, same-collection replacements. The floor operation retains staged nested arrays; every separate edit still passes normal source, identity, review and provenance checks. Any invalid operation rejects the entire candidate.

Missing-geometry requests are shared between local detection and both providers. A valid wall segment does not require an optional footprint; already complete geometry is reused. Missing registration applies to non-reference floors only. These requests guide targeted enrichment, not source completeness judgments. Deterministic IFC generation, reopening and original-coordinate overlays support source review. Existing usable geometry is retained on invalid/rejected replacements. A first model can be published as preview while review runs; preview status is not a fidelity guarantee. Concept styling never enters source counts, QA evidence or IFC facts.

## Conversation and reviewed answers

`AskRequest` contains `document_id`, `question` and optional `revision_id`, `request_id`, `conversation_id`, `reply_to`, `clarification_response`. `conversation_id` is the selected building ID. Async repeated `request_id` reuses its question job. History comes from the server's saved building conversation; client-supplied assistant assertions are not accepted as evidence.

Messages carry `id`, `role`, `revision_id`, `timestamp`, optional job/request/reply references, and either user `question` or assistant `answer`. Clarification replies reference an existing assistant clarification in that building. Earlier answers help resolve phrases such as “the upper floor” but remain fallible context, never additional factual sources.

Intent resolution is separate from source sufficiency. A clarification returns:

```json
{"status":"clarification","answer":"Which floor?","clarification":{"message":"Which floor?","suggestions":["Ground floor","Upper floor","Both"],"free_text_allowed":true},"gate":null,"inspection_passes":0}
```

It has no evidence refusal or reviewed factual draft. Ordinary answers retain `answered|insufficient|unclear`, the three-way sufficiency gate, bounded additional inspection and post-draft review. Answers include `answered_revision_id`, `display_revision_id`, validated original-page `evidence` or native `model_evidence`, conservative `highlight_ids`, `support_summary`, review metadata, and `calculation_results` with source-bound inputs/results. Rejected drafts do not become findings. Chat citations work without 3D and open the exact answered source revision; unreliable geometry associations omit highlights.

Door questions distinguish depicted symbols from all installed building doors. A schedule is not universally required for visible leaves/swings/jambs. Ambiguous openings should be identified individually and connecting doors counted once. Gate, draft and review all apply these rules; generated object totals cannot replace original drawing inspection.

For `sources_only` reasoning, nested `user_provided` calibration/registration/stair connection fields are stripped from the serialized interpretation copy and supplied-value records are omitted. Saved data remains unchanged. Permitted `sources_and_user` answers expose relevant inputs separately, cite `user_value_evidence` IDs and receive server-added `user_value_attributions`; original-source questions cannot silently adopt them.

## Editable inputs and provenance

Assumption rows expose `id`, `scope`, `property`, `label`, `value`, `unit`, `provenance`, `reason`, optional `source`, and `editable`. Provenance distinguishes observed information, inferred interpretations, display assumptions, unknowns and user-provided values. Shared floor assumptions are grouped; source observations are retained separately.

The batch payload is:

```json
{"base_revision_id":"...","edits":[{"property":"floor_height","scope":{"floor_id":"..."},"value":3.4,"unit":"m","reason":"Provided by user"}],"supporting_source_ids":[]}
```

Each edit may also cite `source:{page,bbox,source_id?,source_page?}`. Supporting files must already belong to the building. Implemented properties are:

| Property | Value and scope |
|---|---|
| `floor_height` | Finite positive number; floor scope; `m`, `mm`, `cm`, `ft` or `in`. |
| `display_height` | Positive number; floor scope; physical units above or explicit `relative` display units. |
| `calibration` | `{length:number,segment:[[x,y],[x,y]]}` with distinct normalized endpoints, physical unit and a source region on the selected floor's page. |
| `stair_connection` | Selected stair object/floor; `{target_floor_id,target_feature_id?}` referencing another known floor and optionally its stair. |
| `interpretation_correction` | Nonempty text describing a scoped correction; reviewed through a typed data patch. |

Apply validates the full batch before mutation. Inputs retain their IDs, scope, units, source support, submission/base revision and `user_provided` provenance. Observed source heights are not rewritten as user values. Known source calibration/height conflicts, including section observations with uncertain scope, retain both source facts and submitted inputs and return `needs_attention` without replacing the usable revision. Equivalent calibration is compared using original-page aspect and physical unit conversion.

Numeric changes to an existing scene generate/reopen locally, run loss checks and use one existing original-source/actual-geometry review before publication. The reviewer receives user values separately and must distinguish their authority from source observations. Source-only numeric input persistence does not automatically request 3D. Interpretation corrections invoke the bounded typed-patch workflow. Editing/keystrokes make no model calls. Failed/stopped/rejected candidates retain submitted inputs in the persisted job and preserve the prior usable revision.

A supplied vertical height never establishes XY scale. With unknown horizontal calibration, physical height remains attributed in its original unit; vertical presentation uses the disclosed display convention `1 m = 1.2/2.6 relative units`. The scene stays unscaled. This is a display choice, not an inferred building measurement.

## Geometry, formats and portability

Original-page coordinates, building registration/elevation and viewer-only exploded spacing remain separate. Supported shared-page registration can use relative units without asserting metres. Stacked mode retains generated storey elevations; exploded mode adds spacing. Continuous schematic stairs preserve supported footprints/connectivity with assumed vertical geometry identified. Optional wall footprints preserve supported tapered/angled shapes; explicit hosts remain required for openings.

Native floors come from supplied IFC storeys and containment. Cutaway is a percentage clipping control: 0% is the floor reference and 100% the full reference height. All-floor mode uses each storey's own reference; missing heights and uncontained geometry use displayed fallback references. Clipping does not shrink walls or move openings. Camera, floor/mode selection and assumptions controls survive accepted updates where identities remain valid.

SVG and DXF use the existing normalized-image pipeline, with preserved original bytes, vector/layout metadata and coordinate mappings. Declared document units alone do not establish physical building scale. Unsupported rendering features are reported; external resources are not fetched. DWG is unavailable because no validated converter path exists. See `SOURCE_FORMATS.md` for adapter details.

Portable artifact v5 adds available original source bytes/hashes, mappings, source interpretations and user inputs; V2–V4 remain readable. Legacy derived artifacts may contain only embedded normalized pages with null source IDs and no recoverable original file bytes. Those pages remain authoritative supplied image evidence; absent original files are never fabricated. Upgrading such an artifact to v5 does not recover missing originals. Original pages and derived status are restored on import. Existing per-file/source normalization and artifact-size limits remain explicit; the PDF five-page bound is not a cumulative building-page or DXF-layout bound. An over-capacity portable export must fail explicitly while preserving the local bundle. Large multi-source exports and complex vector semantics are not guaranteed complete reconstruction.
# Reconstruction V3 contract (reviewed)

Root owns shared schema/API/provider and import integration. V3 replaces room-edge enclosure generation with an explicit physical-boundary description. Original-page coordinates, source-only QA, unknown scale and V2 portable imports remain compatible.

## Description

Keep BuildingDescription(floors, limitations) and existing floor source/order/orientation/calibration fields. RoomDescription adds environment indoor|outdoor|unknown; its polygon creates only an IfcSpace footprint, never walls. Add floor.boundaries, floor.features and floor.unresolved. No list caps.

BoundaryDescription: key:str (unique within floor), kind wall|railing|open_edge, label, segment:list[Point], source:PageRegion, thickness_segment:list[Point] (empty if unknown), basis observed|inferred, note. Walls and railings require two segment endpoints; open_edge additionally accepts a continuous polyline rendered as flat strips, never an enclosure. Physical wall records describe one shared wall axis spanning any explicitly hosted gaps; each shared physical boundary is listed once. Thin door leaves, arcs, furniture and annotations are not walls. Explicit railings/open edges never become full-height walls.

OpeningDescription replaces host_room/host_edge with host_wall:str|null (boundary key); retain kind, label, segment, source, basis, note. Segment endpoints identify the actual gap on the wall, not a drawn door leaf or swing arc. Unknown host stays null and yields an unresolved record, never arbitrary attachment. No valid host depends on a room polygon surviving.

FeatureDescription: kind stairs|table|chair|cabinet|bed|sofa|sink|toilet|shower|bath|appliance|other, label, polygon:list[Point], source:PageRegion, basis, note. Every meaningful depicted feature is included, with simple footprint symbols sufficient; no vertical dimension is required. Generic other+label covers features outside the named categories. UnresolvedDescription: label, category:str, source:PageRegion, reason. Use for ambiguous classification or unlocatable geometry; annotations are excluded. Group inseparable repeated symbols explicitly when individual extents cannot be resolved.

## Scene and IFC

SceneElement adds representation reconstructed|schematic|unresolved, semantic_type:str, environment indoor|outdoor|unknown. Extend kind to room/outdoor/wall/railing/open_edge/door/window/stairs/furniture/fixture/other. Unresolved elements have geometry=None but retain stable GlobalId, source, label and note reason. Every described entry must appear as rendered/schematic/unresolved, including validation omissions. Stable namespace keys must not renumber after omission. No silent omission counter as the only record.

Generated spaces are thin plates. Explicit walls use depicted thickness where a valid original segment establishes it, otherwise labeled display width. Openings create actual IfcOpeningElement void/fill relationships; host geometry is checked in aspect-correct coordinates. Reject incompatible/overlapping host associations to unresolved records. Never close a room edge to create a host. Features may be flat schematic IFC solids/symbols; any thickness, height, tread motif or vertical offset is a display assumption. No engineering/step-count claims.

New artifacts use manifest version3/marker v3 and embed the exact BuildingDescription plus all original normalized PNGs and per-element metadata. Reader accepts version2 artifacts without silently reclassifying them as native IFC. Version3 validates new semantic/status fields against per-element Psets, actual IFC classes/storeys and source regions. Unresolved entries use geometry-less semantic entities; all-unresolved scenes are allowed but explicitly state that no 3D geometry was reconstructed; the original source and unresolved inventory remain available. Native IFC import unchanged.

## Comparison UI

Root provides Scene.comparison: list[PlanComparison] computed after actual IFC tessellation. Each entry: element_id, floor_id, page, layer spaces|walls|openings|features|unresolved, polygons:list[list[list[float]]], lines:list[list[list[float]]], method:str, cut_height:float|null. Coordinates are normalized ORIGINAL page. They are inverse-transformed from actual meshes using stored SceneFloor.transform, without viewer explosion offsets. Walls use a horizontal cross-section through the assumed opening height (explicitly labeled display section), other elements use actual footprint projection. Unresolved entries carry no fabricated paths; UI uses element.source.bbox as a visibly different unresolved marker. Recompute on reopening; do not trust stale saved overlay paths.

Frontend adds a comparison control in the original drawing view, layer toggles and overlay opacity. Original orientation remains unchanged. Separate floor/page filtering, source-linked semantic/status counts and unresolved feature list make missing/incorrect features reviewable. Mesh highlights and assumption controls remain independent. Image-answer association may include new valid feature kinds, but unresolved or unrenderable entries cannot receive invented 3D highlights. Original source citations remain available.

## Budget and acceptance

Existing upload/IFC safeguards remain; no new floor/room/feature caps. Larger explicit inventories may exceed the current reconstruction token/time budget; measure live and change reconstruction-only settings if required, after communicating the tradeoff. No changes to gate/answer budgets or automatic provider fallback.

Acceptance requires visual original-coordinate comparison of both unchanged11397 floors and1794, explicit audit of outdoor boundaries, physical shared walls, every clear opening, stairs and furnishing/fixture coverage, plus live source QA/highlights/refusal and portable reopening. Passing mesh validation alone is not fidelity evidence. Record residual unresolved features/omissions honestly.

## Review resolutions
Duplicate boundary keys never resolve by first/last wins: all conflicting records and dependent openings remain unresolved. Invalid item geometry never invents an exact source region: retain a valid explicit item region, otherwise use the valid floor region and label it unlocalized; invalid floor/page references fail. An empty mesh set is a source inventory result, not a successful 3D reconstruction. The frontend uses safe empty bounds and a clear no-geometry notice.

## Final implementation settings

Reconstruction alone uses one Gemini `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` high-thinking request (explicit `GEMINI_RECONSTRUCTION_MODEL` override), 150 seconds and 32,768 output tokens. These are measured hackathon design choices; larger inventories can still fail, and API success is not fidelity acceptance. Answer/crop retain 45 seconds/8,192 tokens; Decisions is unchanged. Temporary OpenAI uses the same reconstruction-only time/token budgets. No automatic fallback, refinement call, manual source edits or new image-processing stage was added.

V3 permits a contextual evidence box to extend beyond its approximate floor region when the same-page boxes overlap with positive area. Actual geometry anchors remain inside both the floor and source region; no source box is silently rewritten. Disjoint/wrong-page regions remain unresolved. V2 portable imports retain their prior containment check.

Room interiors with positive overlap remain unresolved rather than being silently repaired; independent walls/openings/features survive. Empty feature polygons explicitly request a bbox schematic, while malformed supplied polygons remain unresolved. Display stair bands are level symbol marks, never measured tread counts, rise or travel direction.

## Boundary-line citation repair

BoundaryDescription.source now uses BoundaryRegion: area or normalized positive-length line. Other PageRegion/QA contracts remain strict. A line citation must contain the actual boundary segment before the generator adds one-original-page-pixel selection padding to the zero dimension; physical geometry and thickness validation use original coordinates. Original line bounds remain embedded in the exact description; the padded SourceRef carries a selection-only note. Inconsistent associations remain unresolved. See RECONSTRUCTION_502_FIX.md.

## Shared uncalibrated page scale

Uncalibrated floor transforms use a page-derived factor `10/max(page.width/page.height,1)` rather than independently normalizing each floor bbox. Floor boxes affect centering only. This preserves drawn proportions among uncalibrated diagrams on one page; it does not prove physical scale or equal drawing scales, especially for independently resized diagrams. Separate page frames remain schematic. Supported physical calibration is unchanged. New `page_extent` assumptions disclose the convention; the UI checks those markers before making the claim. Existing artifacts retain stored transforms and original IDs; no automatic migration. See FLOOR_SCALE_FIX.md.

## Depicted wall bands and schematic visibility

A supplied boundary segment is a reference line, not necessarily a centerline. A valid perpendicular thickness segment establishes signed face offsets in the aspect-correct source plane. Validate contact before display rotation; extrude between those faces. This retains depicted relative widths at unknown scale. Missing/invalid widths keep explicit display defaults. Supported band contacts form junctions without endpoint snapping or filling positive gaps.

Opening range and normal-offset checks use the same source plane and named host. Gap endpoints retain their longitudinal positions. Void and fill are centered normally within the supported band (or assumed default band), with an explicit placement assumption; voids cut the full band. A previously accepted opening outside the actual supported band is not grandfathered in.

Feature footprints and source classifications remain fallible drawing interpretations. Raised schematics improve visibility without establishing vertical measurements. Relative to the existing assumed wall height H, display heights are table .30H; chair/bed .20H; sofa/sink/toilet .25H; cabinet .50H; appliance .40H; shower/bath/stairs/other .10H. Motifs and dimensions are portable assumptions. Support symbols do not establish leg counts; chair facing and stair ascent/rise/travel direction are not inferred. New geometry must remain inside the existing footprint.

Unresolved canvas annotations are HTML source links, not IFC geometry or answer highlights. Precise source regions use the stored source transform; coarse/unlocalized records use a labeled floor badge. Annotation screen positions may be separated for legibility without changing source coordinates or exported geometry. A more elevated derived-model camera exposes interiors; native IFC camera behavior is unchanged. See SCHEMATIC_FIDELITY_PLAN.md and SCHEMATIC_FIDELITY_RESULTS.md.

# Source-first iteration implementation plan

Status: independently reviewed and approved in round 1; no planning blockers. Reviewer explicitly confirmed source/revision compatibility, optional geometry, unknown-scale supplied heights, cached append, artifact portability and actual-IFC elevation requirements. This plan implements all twelve authoritative attachment requirements; it supersedes older single-source, automatic-reconstruction, new-format exclusion and no-commit instructions where the newer user request differs. Gemini and its configurable reconstruction model remain unchanged. Focused milestone commits are authorized; pushes are not.

## Scope and design choices

Keep the existing one-process FastAPI, plain browser JavaScript, filesystem bundles, original evidence, shared description, deterministic IfcOpenShell generator, reviewed QA and concept renderer. Add automatic source interpretation, explicitly requested optional geometry, incremental multi-source buildings, source-linked conversation/clarification, editable attributed values, coherent floor presentation, diagnostics and a separate format adapter track. Preserve V2–V4 artifacts and saved bundles.

No arbitrary source/object/vertex cap is proposed. Existing per-file normalization/provider/job limits remain visible and must be reported individually; do not reinterpret the historical five-page per-file bound as a five-page whole-building bound. Existing 25 MiB portable IFC bound may prevent embedding large multi-source sets: report that export limitation without losing the local bundle or blocking QA. Existing configured correction/call budgets remain; extraction alone must not spend reconstruction-review/repair calls. Root must communicate any necessary changed budget before live calls. Local resource isolation for SVG/DXF protects the renderer from active content/external resources; it can reject drawings relying on external assets, so report unsupported features explicitly. These are implementation choices, not claims about source validity.

Exclude detailed roofs/domes, photorealism, Blender/cloud rendering, auth/database and autonomous runtime agents. Unknown geometry stays unresolved. SVG and DXF are now included; DWG support depends on an actually verified converter and must never be advertised speculatively.

## Evidence from current implementation

- `BuildingStore.add` uses original SHA256 as building ID and one building-level source/pages manifest; immutable revision files do not yet pin source membership.
- `reconstruct_scene` saves description only after generate/reopen. `build_reasoning` derives drawing objects/floors from scene rather than interpretation.
- `JobRunner` combines extraction, geometry and review, with generic failure text implying an earlier model even on first failure.
- Existing stable IDs, frame registries, atomic CURRENT publication, candidate retention, original-page overlays and source-only drawing QA are reusable.
- `generate_ifc` explicitly gives every floor elevation zero; metric-only alignment disallows supported registration of unscaled diagrams. The viewer already adds an independent exploded offset but cannot repair missing building elevation.
- Existing `segment` plus thickness-band walls cannot faithfully represent every tapered/angled end. Diagnose actual outputs before choosing schema or generator corrections.

## Shared contracts (freeze before dependent implementation)

### Source identity and revision membership

A building keeps its existing 64-hex `building_id` (initial source hash); adding files never changes it. A `source_id` is SHA256 of original bytes, independent of filename. Source metadata includes original bytes/hash, display filename aliases, media kind, normalized page hashes/dimensions, normalization mapping/diagnostics and optional vector metadata. Deduplicate resources and successful interpretation by source identity, including reuse across buildings; do not reuse a source result conditioned on another building's context as independent extraction.

Each immutable revision saves a `sources` manifest. Entries map `(source_id, source_page)` to an append-only building `page` number, with the original normalized page pixels and coordinate mapping. Never renumber earlier pages. Internal `Page` and public page descriptors add `source_id`, `source_page` and source filename; existing `page` remains the canonical legacy selector. A source extraction cache uses source-local pages; merge explicitly remaps every source reference into the building page namespace and assigns building-stable object IDs. Geometry/review caches are keyed to their input revision, not merely original file hash.

References retain existing `{page,bbox}` and add optional `source_id`/`source_page`; server resolves legacy refs against that revision's manifest and rejects conflicting combinations. Every normalized bbox remains in the displayed original page frame, never the building frame. New evidence URLs are revision-pinned; existing unversioned routes remain compatibility/current routes. An older answer resolves its own source manifest, not CURRENT's source list. Legacy bundles synthesize one source entry on load without rewriting old revisions.

Native IFC keeps original GlobalId/property evidence per `source_id`; model record identity must include source identity when different IFCs repeat a GlobalId. Drawing-derived IFC restores drawing sources and cannot enter native factual shortcuts. Multi-source drawing ingestion is the main UI flow; mixed/native source catalogs retain per-record evidence rules rather than converting native objects to floor polygons. Never silently overwrite or fuse conflicting source facts.

### Shared interpretation with optional geometry

Extend `BuildingDescription` additively, not with a second incompatible reasoning pipeline. Retain floors, original labels, source refs and existing persistent IDs. Allow semantic records without geometric traces: empty/absent polygon/segment fields mean geometry unavailable, not empty evidence. Add source-linked observations/measurements for all view types, including section/elevation facts; only actual floor plans instantiate floor geometry. Expose extraction coverage and per-source completion. Preserve exact returned validated interpretation before any generator call.

Provider interface: `extract_interpretation(document, *, include_geometry=False)` returns the shared schema. The source-first prompt requests useful semantic observations, view classification, labels, measurements and evidence regions without exhaustive wall/feature polygon tracing. Geometry action reuses that interpretation and requests only missing geometry/relationships through the same schema and typed patch workflow; existing full descriptions require no re-extraction. Existing `reconstruct` may remain a compatibility wrapper. Reasoning object/floor records derive from saved interpretation independent of scene; optional scene associations enrich them without becoming factual evidence.

Source extraction operates independently per new source so adding B does not re-extract A. Building integration combines cached source interpretations deterministically; repeated views of a floor must not silently create additional storeys. Merge only source-supported floor equivalences, retain all supporting refs, and mark uncertain alternatives/conflicting dimensions explicitly. Explicit geometry/refinement can inspect multiple originals for cross-source relationships/conflicts. Persist interpretation identity/provenance and missing geometry; no geometry work or reconstruction review on default extraction. Missing interpretation records never establish missing source objects.

Revision payload adds `interpretation_status`, `geometry_status`, and `geometry_revision_id` where retained geometry belongs to an older interpretation. QA pins the current source/interpretation revision; UI explicitly identifies any retained older model, and highlights only validated associations. Publication of extraction must never relabel an older scene as regenerated against new evidence. Successful JSON survives a geometry error, restart or stop. Source-only revisions are first-class successes.

### Jobs, atomicity and APIs

Keep current routes. `POST /api/documents` accepts existing `file` and additive multi-file `files`; source-first upload queues automatic extraction server-side for genuinely uncached drawing sources. `POST /api/buildings/{id}/sources` adds related files to the selected building. Return source list, per-source statuses, extraction job IDs, revision identity and `has_scene`. A duplicate upload/reopen returns cached state without inference; interrupted or failed extraction requires an explicit retry, not surprise reprocessing.

Add `POST /api/buildings/{id}/extraction` for explicit retry. Existing reconstruction endpoint is the explicit Generate 3D/Refine action. Coalesce repeated requests for the same source/operation. Persist source additions before launching inference. Workers extract against immutable source snapshots and save cache results even if their publication base became stale. Independently reviewed plan; review resolutions are in RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md. ## Diagnosis grounded in the saved final artifacts

Inspected the unchanged original `colorful-11397.png`, `/tmp/junction-live-v2-final/colorful-11397.png.ifc`, its matching scene JSON and the saved viewer image. The final IFC and scene agree: two storeys, 11 spaces, 57 walls, one door, no windows, and no stairs/furnishing elements. Every scene element has a mesh. Two terrace/balcony spaces are represented as ordinary rooms with ten automatically generated perimeter walls. These are actual IFC modeling/description limitations, not missing viewer meshes.

The current generator turns every retained room polygon edge into a wall. Room polygons describe usable spaces, not a structural wall inventory: this invents enclosure on outdoor edges, can duplicate shared boundaries and can turn a mistaken door-leaf/arc-shaped room boundary into a wall. In the inspected final artifact the diagonal wall centerlines are on the exterior-space outlines; we have not established that this exact run traced a door leaf. The design nevertheless permits that failure and must stop deriving walls from room perimeters.

The schema cannot represent indoor/outdoor distinctions, independent boundaries, stairs, tables, cabinets or sanitary objects. The current prompt requests only selected openings, and opening hosts depend on retained room-edge indices; invalid/omitted room polygons can therefore remove otherwise visible openings. Some failed openings are summarized only as a count. The result cannot account for meaningful unrendered features individually.

The separate `/tmp/medium-quality-description.json` is another run: two floor records, 12 room records and four opening records. It is useful evidence of extraction coverage, but cannot explain individual omissions or geometry in the final IFC above. The saved final `1794` artifact has six spaces, 30 walls, five doors and two windows; use it as a regression baseline, not a ground-truth inventory.

## Narrow description changes (root finalizes contract)

Keep named x/y and left/top/right/bottom on the wire, original-page coordinates internally, existing floor regions/transforms/calibration/alignment/measurements, and medium reconstruction reasoning unless controlled live evidence warrants another choice. Extend each floor with the following compact records; no new arbitrary list caps.

- `rooms`: retain label/polygon/basis/note; add `environment: indoor|outdoor|unknown`. These produce footprint plates only. Unknown classification remains visible; it does not authorize enclosure. A terrace/balcony footprint is allowed without known elevation, floor thickness or railing height.
- `boundaries`: local stable `key`, `kind: wall|railing|open_edge`, label, original-page segment, source region, `thickness_segment` (empty if unknown), basis and concise note. One record per physical segment, shared by neighbouring spaces. Trace the depicted wall/railing itself; never door leaves, swing arcs, furniture edges or inferred room rectangles. Keep width/extrusion as current explicit display assumptions unless a valid thickness segment supplies depicted width. An open edge is recorded as open; it must not produce a wall.
- `openings`: retain door/window kind, label, original segment, source region and basis/note; replace `host_room/host_edge` with `host_wall: boundary key|null`. The host must be the correct same-floor explicit wall. Missing/ambiguous hosting is unresolved, not a guessed nearest wall. Unknown height/sill is compatible with a schematic opening and an explicit display assumption.
- `features`: `kind: stairs|table|chair|cabinet|bed|sofa|sink|toilet|shower|bath|appliance|other`, label, source region, polygon, basis and note. Source polygons may be approximate footprint symbols; unresolved geometry belongs in the unresolved list. Do not discard a visible object solely because its vertical dimensions are unknown. Stairs may be a low schematic footprint/tread indication; do not infer an actual rise, direction or connection between floors. Distinguish object geometry from the walls that surround it.
- `unresolved`: label, category, original source region and reason for visible but unclassifiable features or uncertain geometry. Server validation failures must produce equivalent persistent outcomes, not disappear into a warning count. Avoid duplicating the same item in feature and unresolved input lists. Group inseparable repeated symbols explicitly when individual source extents cannot be resolved.

Keep extraction to the existing bounded request. Ask the model to account for the meaningful depicted categories across each entire floor, including openings and furnishings, without restricting it to a few illustrative examples. Model omissions are not automatically detectable: the inventory is a reconstruction audit aid, not a certified complete list or factual count source. Meaningful feature coverage needs a source-by-source visual acceptance pass.

## Deterministic generator behavior

1. Validate spaces, boundaries, openings and features independently. Invalid room polygons must not suppress valid explicit walls or openings. Existing room conflict rules remain within each floor; do not repair polygons or infer missing structural partitions.
2. Emit footprint plates for indoor/outdoor spaces with distinct provenance/classification and viewer styling. Emit IfcWall only from explicit wall records; emit railing geometry only from explicit railing records. Open edges remain visibly open. Shared boundary IDs map to one wall. Exact repeated/reversed copies can be recognized and reported; conflicting or uncertain duplicate interpretations remain unresolved rather than arbitrarily choosing one or silently merging nearby geometry. Duplicate/conflicting local boundary keys must never resolve by array order: mark the conflicting records and dependent openings unresolved unless identity is unambiguous.
3. Attach door/window void/fill relations only to their validated wall ID. Validate original endpoints/source bbox/floor consistency and the existing host-wall-band projection. Keep actual boolean openings in the IFC, rather than painting symbols on solid walls. If hosting fails, retain that exact opening as an unresolved inventory/source item. No automatic migration to a neighbouring wall and no widening source regions to force acceptance.
4. Generate simple, visibly differentiated feature geometry. Tables/cabinets may use IfcFurnishingElement, sanitary features an appropriate supported IFC product or generic furnishing subtype, and stairs a schematic product/footprint rather than a fabricated inter-storey connector. A small set of deterministic primitives is enough; this is not an asset library or detailed furniture modeling project. Record all display heights, thicknesses and other absent dimensions as assumptions.
5. Give every extracted/validated item a persistent compressed IFC GlobalId in its floor namespace. Persist its category, source, resolution status and reason. Unresolved entries become geometry-less semantic IFC entities with matching scene records; they have no invented mesh or location beyond their valid original source region. If malformed coordinates prevent reliable localization, use the known floor region explicitly marked coarse/unlocalized; do not manufacture a precise bounding box. Stable IDs survive validation omissions, caching and download/reopen. These inventories remain explicitly derived, never authoritative building counts.

Replace “at least one room must survive” with the reviewed contract's “at least one supported renderable element”: usable explicit walls/features may survive room interpretation failure. All-unresolved results remain explicit no-3D failures; do not claim a model was built. Root should retain the extraction/unresolved diagnostic payload for inspection when possible. This changes a current invariant and must be communicated; it is not a new feature-count limit.

## Source overlay must compare the actual IFC

Root's `app/comparison.py` computes the comparison from tessellated generated IFC meshes (and actual hosted void/fill geometry when needed), transformed back through the inverse stored floor matrix to the original page. The frontend places those vectors on the unchanged source image with separate layers for boundaries, indoor/outdoor footprints, openings, schematic features and unresolved regions. The overlay must not simply redraw the model's intended polygons or bounding boxes and call that a geometry check.

A full-height wall footprint projection hides opening cuts because the lintel above an opening projects over the gap. Either use appropriate mesh cross-sections or explicitly overlay actual IFC opening/fill footprints alongside projected wall footprints, with a clear legend. Do not claim that an uncut projection proves opening correctness. Compare multiple original floor regions on the same image without applying viewer explosion or display rotation to the source. Native source clicks, floor filtering and restored embedded pages must continue to work.

The UI should make unresolved items inspectable individually: selecting one shows its original region and reason. Show concise category/status totals for navigation, labeled as reconstruction inventory, not building facts. The user can inspect broad coverage without reading a long warning paragraph or searching only a selected set of doors.

## Design constraints to explain before implementation

- Independent explicit wall extraction replaces a wrong inference, but adds description content. The current token budget may then be exhausted; token-limit/provider failures remain operational errors. Run both live originals early. - Missing physical heights do not block schematic reconstruction. Assumptions remain visible and cannot answer factual height questions. Unknown scale, orientation, registration and inter-floor elevations retain current semantics.
- Source/host/geometry checks can leave clearly visible features unresolved. They must remain in the portable inventory and overlay, with reasons. This may still block visual acceptance if major recognizable features are absent; a successful HTTP status alone is not success.
- Existing upload, IFC byte/element/triangle and response safeguards remain. Additional source-linked features increase artifact size; oversized artifacts fail explicitly rather than silently dropping features/pages.
- Schematic feature silhouettes are sufficient for this hackathon. No new file formats, hidden-floor inference, structural completeness, parametric CAD editing, photorealism, cloud rendering or extra agent runtime.

## Shared action boundary

`POST /api/chat/actions` interprets and validates intent only. It does not run QA, save refinements, generate geometry, or introduce a job runner. The browser executes validated actions through existing operations.

Request: `{message,request_id,document_id?,revision_id?,workspace:{geometry_revision_id?,view_mode,selected_ids,focused_id,camera,tour,highlighting,show_assumptions}}`. Implement the next hackathon iteration around source-first reasoning and coherent building reconstruction. The following changes were discussed in a side conversation and should not be assumed implemented.

Use the established planning, independent plan review, bounded implementation and independent implementation review workflow. Reviewers should directly interact with the browser and compare actual reopened IFC geometry with original drawings. Make focused commits at suitable milestones; do not push.

1. Make reasoning extraction independent of optional 3D generation

The default flow should be:

Upload → preserve original sources → extract and save reasoning JSON
                                              ├─→ Question answering
                                              └─→ Optional 3D generation

Start structured extraction automatically after upload. Save valid interpretation JSON as soon as extraction completes, before IFC generation. QA must be able to use it without a 3D model. Skipping or failing geometry generation must not discard successful extraction.

Make 3D generation an explicit user action. Reuse the existing interpretation and obtain additional geometry only where needed. Keep one shared representation with optional geometry information rather than separate, incompatible pipelines.

To reduce token cost, the no-render path should skip geometry-specific model work and reconstruction review/repair calls. IfcOpenShell generation and Three.js rendering are local and do not themselves consume model tokens.

For drawings, QA and Decisions must continue to inspect original images alongside the fallible JSON. Missing extracted records must not be mistaken for missing source evidence. Questions asked before extraction finishes should remain answerable from the originals.

2. Preserve caching and incremental reuse

Inspect and retain the existing content-based persistence. Reuploading identical bytes, including under another filename, should reuse saved resources without repeating inference.

Persist interpretation JSON independently of rendering. Keep original files, source mappings, successful extraction, geometry and review results through failures and restart. Explicit retries or refinement can make new calls; reopening, orbiting and mode switching must not.

Adding another source to a building should reuse existing extraction rather than process every unchanged file again. Ordinary question answering may still incur token usage; adding answer caching is outside this iteration.

3. Diagnose the colorful-34.png failure

Use the unchanged original:

assets/junction-dataset/data/cubicasa5k/colorful-34.png

It currently reports:

> Source processing failed operationally. Previous usable revision retained; no evidence-quality conclusion was made.

Determine the actual failed stage and exception through controlled live testing. Do not guess whether the cause is Gemini, schema validation, IFC generation or reopening. Retain returned structured descriptions safely for deterministic replay where possible.

Improve stage-specific diagnostics without exposing credentials or raw requests. When no model has ever existed, say that the source was saved but no model was generated; do not imply that a previous usable model was retained.

4. Investigate unnecessary door-count refusal

The application refused a door-count question by demanding a complete door schedule, clearer symbols and comprehensive legends, although door leaves and swing arcs are visible.

Inspect the initial sufficiency decision, draft and post-draft review to determine where that unnecessary requirement arose. Do not assume Decisions alone caused it.

Distinguish counting doors depicted in the supplied plans from establishing every installed door in the actual building. A door schedule is not a universal prerequisite for counting visible symbols.

Return a supported count with source regions when possible. Identify genuinely ambiguous openings individually and explain whether they affect the total. Avoid double-counting a connecting door from its two adjacent spaces. Preserve appropriate uncertainty rather than forcing an exact answer.

This must work from original drawings even when reconstruction fails. Generated IFC object counts must never substitute for factual drawing inspection. Add positive door-count and genuinely ambiguous-opening regression cases; keep evaluation annotations out of runtime context.

5. Provide consistent native IFC floor controls and adjustable cutaway

For duplex_arc.ifc, expose floor selection using supplied storeys and containment relationships. Native IFC should receive the relevant inspection controls already available for generated models.

Replace the binary cutaway with a percentage slider. Define its reference clearly—for example, 0% at the selected storey’s floor level and 100% at full storey height—and make all-floor behavior understandable. Clip geometry rather than shrinking walls or moving openings. Any unsupported reference height remains a display assumption.

6. Assemble drawing-derived floors into one coherent building

For unchanged colorful-11397.png, investigate the lateral offset and the collapse of floors into one plane when vertical separation is disabled.

Separate original page coordinates, building placement and exploded-view offsets. The diagrams’ positions on the sheet must not automatically determine their positions in the building.

Use supported shared features, especially the staircase and exterior boundaries, to register corresponding floors. Preserve their differing footprints, including the larger terrace. Do not independently rescale floors or force equal footprints.

Stacked mode should retain storey elevations; exploded mode should add extra spacing. Where heights are unknown, use explicit display assumptions without presenting them as measured dimensions. Preserve the shared-page scale fix and keep uncertain cross-page scale relationships explicit.

Corresponding stairs should connect the storeys where the source supports that relationship. A simple continuous schematic connection is sufficient; missing rise measurements should not erase clearly depicted connectivity. Preserve supported footprints and label assumed vertical geometry.

7. Diagnose wall shapes and unresolved hosted openings

Inspect the actual description, host associations, transforms and reopened IFC behind messages such as:

> Opening cannot be projected within its explicit host band and original source region.

Determine whether the extraction selected the wrong host, misplaced a wall/opening, misrepresented thickness or introduced inconsistent coordinates. Clear source doorways should prompt correction of the responsible records, not arbitrary attachment to a nearby wall.

Compare the red wall overlays against the actual black wall footprints. The source contains genuinely thick and tapered/angled wall ends; do not assume every unusual shape is erroneous or replace all walls with constant-width rectangles.

Use building-level consistency checks to identify contradictions in walls, openings, storeys and stairs. These checks should guide source inspection and correction, without inventing a “perfect” building from unsupported information.

Support uploading several related blueprints together and adding sources to an existing building. Use a suitable kit_institute dataset example if available.

Plans, sections and elevations should contribute their supported information without every view becoming a floor. Preserve file identity, original page coordinates, citations and source-specific authority. Expose conflicting measurements or uncertain alignment.

Replace the isolated question/result interaction with a lightweight chat scoped to the selected building. Preserve conversation context so follow-up questions such as “What about the upper floor?” can resolve their references.

When ambiguity materially changes the answer, Gemini should ask a brief clarification, preferably with selectable suggestions and a free-text option. For example:

> “Do you mean the ground floor, upper floor, or both?”

- Inspected blueprint regions or original IFC records.
- Supported calculations and their inputs.
- A concise explanation of what supports the answer.
- Remaining uncertainty and review outcome.

This should expose useful, evidence-based explanations rather than promise a stream of the model’s private internal reasoning. Do not present unreviewed drafts as final findings.

Citations and object references should connect the conversation to the left-hand viewer. Blueprint references open the original file/page/region; reliable model associations highlight corresponding objects. Respect the selected view and preserve camera controls. If an object mapping is uncertain or 3D is unavailable, the source citation must still work.

Keep original evidence authoritative throughout follow-ups. Earlier assistant messages and extracted JSON are fallible context, not new factual sources. Associate answers with their building revision and preserve access to the evidence used for older answers.

Provide a clean, source-linked table for reconstruction assumptions and unresolved inputs. Distinguish:

- Information observed in the supplied sources.
- Inferred interpretations.
- Display assumptions.
- Unknown information.
- Values supplied by the user.

Group shared assumptions—such as a floor’s display height—rather than presenting hundreds of duplicate rows. Each editable entry should identify the affected floor/object, property, current value or unknown state, units, and why the value was assumed. Selecting an entry should locate its source region and associated geometry where available.

Allow users to provide missing information or correct an interpretation, with an optional supporting document or source region. For example, they could supply a storey height, a known plan distance for calibration, or clarify a stair connection.

User-provided information must retain its provenance. A supplied height should be labeled “provided by user,” not silently converted into a dimension observed in the blueprint. QA may use it with explicit attribution when appropriate; questions about what the drawing itself establishes must retain that distinction. A known vertical height must not automatically establish horizontal plan scale.

Let users edit several entries and submit them through an explicit Apply and refine action. Do not make model calls on every keystroke. Applying changes should:

1. Validate values, units, scope and revision.
2. Preserve the submitted information with its provenance.
3. Review conflicts with existing sources.
4. Refine affected geometry using the existing bounded workflow.
5. Retain the previous usable revision if the candidate fails.
6. Publish an accepted update without resetting exploration.

Preserve user-provided values and their attribution through saving, export and reopening. This is structured input to deterministic generation—not permission to execute user- or model-generated code.

Verify clarification and follow-up QA without any 3D model, clickable chat evidence in both views, and a user-supplied reconstruction value producing a traceable revision. Unsupported source-height questions must still refuse when the original drawing supplies no height, even if a display assumption or user-provided value is available.

Do not optimize the pipeline around a closed list of demo images. Keep known failures as regression tests, and regularly evaluate fresh examples at meaningful implementation milestones—particularly after changes to extraction prompts, schemas, geometry generation or QA.

Vary the inputs across:

- Residential, commercial, institutional and religious buildings.
- Clean drawings, scans, handwritten annotations and sparse plans.
- Rotated diagrams, irregular footprints, multiple floors and multiple related files.
- Dimensioned and unscaled drawings.
- Floor plans, sections, elevations and mixed drawing sets.
- Native IFC and drawing-derived IFC, preserving their different evidence rules.

Select examples from different buildings, not merely different pages or versions of buildings already tested. Maintain a rotating held-out sample. Once a failure informs an implementation change, retain it as a regression case and choose new unseen examples for subsequent generalization checks.

Use the same application pipeline for every case. Avoid filename-specific behavior, hardcoded coordinates, building-specific prompts or manually repaired artifacts presented as successful extraction. Dataset reference answers remain evaluation-only.

Evaluate stages separately:

- Source ingestion and structured extraction.
- Useful QA before or without 3D.
- Grounded answers, appropriate clarification and unnecessary refusals.
- Geometry fidelity, floor relationships, openings and feature coverage.
- Provenance, caching, refinement and recovery from failures.
- Latency and token usage.

Include direct visual comparisons and independent browser inspection. Successful API calls, valid IFC files and higher object counts do not establish fidelity.

Use representative live checks within explicitly communicated budgets rather than rerunning the entire dataset after every edit. Report the selection, failures and limitations so demo-case success cannot conceal broader weaknesses.

The goal is robust handling of arbitrary inputs within the supported formats and documented limits. Complete reconstruction will not always be justified. When information is missing or a view cannot be reconstructed reliably, the pipeline should still preserve usable evidence, answer supported questions, identify unresolved portions and request targeted clarification where useful. It should neither crash generically nor invent a complete building.

12. Add remaining file formats through an independent implementation track

Assign a dedicated subagent an isolated worktree, with agreed interfaces and file ownership, so format support can progress alongside the core work. Integrate through independent review. Coordinate dependency changes with the orchestrator.

Start with SVG:

Add source/proposal picking and disclosure, footprint containment/fallback, a keyed decoration ledger, offscreen preparation and atomic viewer swaps. Preserve camera, target, modes, floor, separation, cutaway, assumptions and surviving selections. Never mutate reasoning/export data.

Store original bytes/pages, descriptions/native records, reasoning, IFC, scene, mappings, assumptions, findings and pipeline metadata. Restore existing artifact IDs and exact descriptions. 3. Backend owns shared reasoning and native IFC extraction: complete semantic identity catalog including geometry-less objects, properties/quantities/units, supplied relationships, explicitly calculated summaries, missing/coverage records and original references. Drawings keep fallible interpretations plus original visual evidence; generated IFC never becomes native factual evidence.
4. Root owns the lightweight background runner/API; backend owns model review/patch hooks and actual-IFC overlay images. Planner and independent reviewer approved checkpoint 1 and the full plan after one clarification round. Reviewers do not implement their own reviewed paths. Root owns contracts/commits. Each retry must:
- Inspect additional evidence.
- Correct a calculation.
- Repair a citation.
- Remove an unsupported claim.
- Or narrow the answer appropriately.

Rephrasing the same unsupported assertion until it receives approval is not progress.

Decisions provides a routing judgment, not a written critique. The reasoning model identifies the correction using original evidence and concrete validation failures.

A wrong room count can be corrected. An actual ceiling height absent from the supplied material cannot be recovered through repeated reasoning.

7. Publish with validated associations.

Show the answer, citations, limitations and reliably associated highlights.

Uncertain object mappings retain source evidence without invented highlights. A missing highlight must not suppress an otherwise supported textual answer.

If reconstruction changed during the request, revalidate highlight associations against the displayed revision. Original source citations remain available even if an earlier object mapping no longer works.

During Q&A, show progress such as:
- “Inspecting source.”
- “Checking answer.”

The model remains usable while the answer is prepared. Questions do not automatically trigger reconstruction.

SHARED EVIDENCE BOUNDARIES

- Original IFC records support answers about the supplied model; they are not proof of as-built reality.
- Drawing-derived IFC remains an interpretation, including after export and reopening.
- Unknown scale stays explicitly unscaled.
- Extrusion heights, decorative materials and proposed furnishings remain assumptions.
- Actual-height questions still refuse when the original source supplies no height.
- Concept additions never become factual evidence merely because they are visible.
- API failures are operational errors, not evidence-quality judgments.
- Missing information is scoped to the inspected material.
- Optional similar-building ideas remain explicitly hypothetical proposals.
- A reviewer’s approval is corroboration, not proof of correctness.
- Model confidence must not be presented as measured accuracy on this dataset.
- Dataset ground-truth answers remain evaluation-only and never become runtime context.

Read its docs/CONCEPT_VISUALIZATION.md, inspect the implementation, verification artifacts and actual git state.

Reuse its existing Three.js concept layer. Keep the simpler inspection mode as the evidence-oriented view.

Do not build a replacement concept renderer or add Blender, remote rendering, new rendering services or downloaded asset libraries for this goal.

The concept worktree reportedly contains:

- Procedural furnishings and planting.
- Glazing.

Its prior verification is useful context, not proof that it works with the current main-thread implementation.

Identify the presentation-specific changes and integrate them carefully. Do not replace newer reconstruction, provenance, scaling, opening, schematic geometry or QA fixes with the concept worktree’s older baseline.

Preserve unrelated work and inspect uncommitted changes before integrating anything.

Maintain these boundaries:
- Inspection and concept consume the same building revision and object mapping.
- Concept styling and decorative proposals never enter factual QA context, source object counts, evidence citations or exported IFC.
- Source-associated furnishings and newly proposed decorations are visibly distinguishable.
- Selecting a proposal identifies it as a proposal.
- Generic semantic categories must not silently imply unsupported specificity. An unspecified appliance must not automatically become a hob.
- Inspect rotated and irregular footprints. Avoid decorative geometry extending outside its supported footprint because of world-axis bounding-box placement.
- If precise styling is unavailable, use an explicit schematic fallback.

- Rebuild affected presentation assets offscreen and publish revisions atomically.

- Check performance on available hardware and report software-rendering limitations honestly.

Blender remains a possible future consumer of the same saved geometry and source mappings. It is outside this implementation goal.

PERSISTENCE AND BACKGROUND PROCESSING

Implement the smallest local persistence mechanism sufficient for the product.

A filesystem artifact store and a lightweight job runner are acceptable. A database, distributed queue or general-purpose agent framework is not required.

Store complete, versioned building bundles containing:
- Original source files and normalized pages.
- Exact building descriptions or native IFC extraction records.
- Reasoning JSON with provenance and coverage information.
- IFC artifacts.
- Browser geometry.
- Stable object mappings and source-coordinate transforms.
- Assumptions and unresolved issues.
- Review findings and revision status.
- Pipeline, prompt and model configuration.

Recognize repeat uploads by content identity rather than filename.

Reopening a saved building must survive application restart without reconstruction. Camera movement, mode changes and questions must not regenerate geometry.

Improved pipelines create explicit new revisions instead of silently overwriting the previous usable result.

A failed background job must not destroy a usable building bundle. Report failure separately from model completeness and source sufficiency.

IMPLEMENTATION SEQUENCE

First inspect the current repository and concept worktree, then produce a small implementation plan and shared contracts.

Use the established planning and independent review workflow. Obtain independent plan review before dependent implementation.

Use staged checkpoints:

1. Integrate the concept view while preserving current inspection and QA.
2. Establish persistent bundles, stable identities and revision-safe viewer updates.
3. Implement or extend native IFC extraction into the shared reasoning interface, preserving drawing-specific evidence behavior.
4. Implement background reconstruction with first-preview publication, source/geometry review and targeted description patches.
5. Add post-draft Q&A review and corrective iteration using the structured reasoning context while retaining the existing sufficiency gate and deterministic validation.
6. Verify the integrated flows with real artifacts and live Gemini, resolve blocking review findings, and document remaining limitations.

Parallelize only tasks with clear file ownership and settled interfaces.

Development subagents are for implementation and review. The application itself does not need a general-purpose multi-agent runtime.

PROVIDER AND EXECUTION POLICY

Gemini remains the final-demo provider.

Preserve the explicit provider switch and current reconstruction-model default. The Hydrogen experiment was not adopted. Do not reopen model selection as part of this goal without concrete evidence that it blocks implementation.

Use existing credentials for live tests necessary to establish compatibility and acceptance. Do not print secrets or raw sensitive requests.

Background reconstruction need not inherit a synchronous HTTP request deadline.

Inspect existing limits and choose explicit, configurable execution budgets appropriate to background reconstruction and interactive QA.

Before introducing or changing a self-imposed constraint, communicate:

- Why it is needed.
- Whether it is an external requirement or our design choice.

This requires communication, not a blanket approval process.

Do not silently introduce arbitrary feature, floor, room or vertex caps.

Avoid unlimited retry loops. Track material progress, repeated feedback and candidate revisions.

Budget exhaustion, API failure and evidence insufficiency remain distinct outcomes. Exhaustion means processing stopped; it does not prove information is absent.

VERIFICATION AND ACCEPTANCE

Use unchanged:

The independent reviewer must directly interact with the browser and inspect original-source overlays, rather than relying only on implementer summaries.

Demonstrate:
