- A source-backed correction produces an updated model without resetting the camera, floor, mode or controls.
- Inserting or reordering description objects does not change unrelated IDs.
- Failed or clearly regressive candidates do not replace a usable revision.
- No invented floors or factual dimensions appear through refinement.
- Original source evidence remains inspectable in inspection and concept modes.
- Saved buildings reopen after application restart without an extraction call.
- Concept proposals remain separate from factual evidence and IFC export.
- A genuine uploaded IFC is extracted into reasoning JSON with original-record provenance.

- Relevant geometry-less IFC entities remain available to reasoning.
# Source-first contract

Implemented checkpoint, 2026-11-14. This extends `CONTRACT.md`, `PRODUCT_PLAN.md` and the reviewed `SOURCE_FIRST_PLAN.md`; final acceptance is tracked separately in `SOURCE_FIRST_VERIFICATION.md`. JSON uses snake_case. The configurable reconstruction default remains `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`; Gemini remains the final-demo provider, with explicit `AI_PROVIDER=openai` compatibility and no automatic failover.

## Sources, identities and revisions

The building ID remains the SHA-256 identity of its initial upload. Each source has its own SHA-256 `source_id`, independent of filename. Original bytes and normalized pages are preserved in filesystem resources; filenames can be aliases. A revision pins its source membership, source-local page mappings, interpretation, identity/frame registries, user inputs and available geometry. A building retains its identity when sources are appended.

Each public page has `page`, `source_id`, `source_page`, `source_filename`, `width`, `height` and `image_url`. `page` is the append-only building page number; `source_page` is the page/layout within that file. Regions use normalized decimal fractions from 0 to 1 in the original displayed page. Pixels, percentages and 0–1000 integer coordinates are rejected, not silently divided. Referenced `page`, `source_id` and `source_page` must agree. Existing page-only references resolve against their pinned revision.

Resources store successful independent per-source interpretations. A cache merge remaps every local page reference into the selected building and assigns building-specific stable IDs. Adding B does not re-extract A. Reopening, renamed byte-identical uploads, orbiting and mode switching do not invoke inference. Failed/interrupted extraction requires explicit retry. Ordinary questions are not answer-cached. Complete retained legacy descriptions are reused; missing new cache fields do not themselves require another inference call.

Possible repeated floor views are conservative: normalized word-contained labels (for example `Erdgeschoss` and `Grundriss Erdgeschoss`) or the same explicitly supported order retain the incoming diagram as a source-linked unresolved alternate view and preserve its semantic observations. This avoids silently creating another storey; it does not establish equivalence or fuse their geometry. Uncertain alignment and differing measurements remain attributed.

**Grouping limitation:** genuine native IFC must be opened as a separate building. Grouping it with another source/native IFC is rejected before publishing a mixed bundle. This is a lean implementation limitation: the current combined drawing pipeline does not supply a complete mixed native-record catalog. Drawing-derived IFC retains drawing authority and can contribute recoverable embedded original sources. Native IFC still uses its complete supplied semantic catalog, including geometry-less records; generated IFC never becomes factual native evidence.

## Public document and job state

Public documents retain prior fields and add `sources`, `interpretation_status`, `geometry_status` and `geometry_revision_id`. `interpretation_status` is `pending`, `partial` or `complete`. Geometry is `not_requested`, `available` or `stale`. `has_scene` means a saved scene exists, not that every source feature has geometry or the model is accurate. After source changes, a retained scene can belong to `geometry_revision_id` rather than the current interpretation revision; it must not be presented as regenerated geometry.

Job kinds are `extraction`, `reconstruction`, `question` and `refinement`. Statuses are `queued`, `running`, `complete`, `needs_attention`, `failed`, `budget_exhausted`, `stopped` and `interrupted`. Jobs include identity, building/base/current revision, phase, message, timestamps, issues and attempts; usage and operation-specific results appear when available. Failure fields include `error_stage`, `error_category`, `diagnostic_id`, safe `diagnostic_message` and `has_previous_model`. A failure with no usable model says sources were saved and no usable model was generated. Valid saved interpretation survives geometry failure.

Returned structured responses may be retained privately for replay; raw provider requests, credentials and exception bodies are not logged or exposed. Stop prevents late publication; an in-flight call may finish. Revision compare-and-swap, guarded publication and per-source merging prevent a late extraction/geometry result from dropping appended sources or user inputs. Restart marks unfinished jobs interrupted while preserving sources and accepted revisions.

## HTTP endpoints

| Method and path | Request / result |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/documents` | Multipart legacy `file` and/or repeated `files`. Returns public document plus `is_new_upload`, `added_source_ids`, `extraction_jobs`. New uncached drawing sources automatically queue interpretation; no automatic 3D. |
| `POST /api/buildings/{id}/sources` | Same multipart fields, append to selected building; same result shape. |
| `GET /api/buildings` | `{buildings:[public_document]}`. |
| `GET /api/buildings/{id}` | Public document plus persisted `jobs`, newest first. |
| `POST /api/buildings/{id}/extraction` | `{source_ids?:[id], retry:true}`; HTTP 202 `{jobs:[job]}`. Successful existing interpretation is reused; failed/interrupted sources can retry. |
| `POST /api/buildings/{id}/reconstruction` | `{base_revision_id?, mode:"refine"|"reconstruct"}`; HTTP 202 job. Explicit geometry generation/refinement. |
| `GET /api/jobs/{id}` | Persisted job and final `answer` for completed questions. |
| `POST /api/jobs/{id}/stop` | Updated stop status. |
| `GET /api/buildings/{id}/revisions/{revision}/pages/{page}` | Exact revision-pinned normalized PNG. A page added later is unavailable in an older revision. |
| `GET /api/documents/{id}/pages/{page}` | Compatibility current-page PNG route. |
| `GET /api/buildings/{id}/sources/{source_id}/original` | Preserved original bytes as attachment; no raw SVG is embedded in the browser. |
| `GET /api/buildings/{id}/revisions/{revision}/evidence/{object_id}` | Original native IFC record and coverage for the pinned revision; rejects drawing-derived factual shortcuts. |
| `GET /api/documents/{id}/scene` | Saved scene; 404 if none. |
| `POST /api/documents/{id}/scene` | Compatibility explicit synchronous generation with `{page:1}`; uses the job workflow and reuses an existing scene. The page argument does not restrict whole-building generation. |
| `GET /api/documents/{id}/model.ifc` | Saved IFC download; 404 before generation. |
| `GET /api/buildings/{id}/conversation` | `{conversation_id:id,messages:[...]}`. |
| `POST /api/questions` | `AskRequest`; HTTP 202 revision-pinned question job. |
| `POST /api/ask` | Compatibility synchronous `AskRequest` → final `Answer`; also persists turns. |
| `GET /api/buildings/{id}/assumptions` | `{building_id,revision_id,rows,editable_properties}`. |
| `POST /api/buildings/{id}/refinements` | Batch request below; HTTP 202 job. |

Expanded failed-job details show only the existing sanitized `diagnostic_message`, escaped as text; raw provider errors and requests are never displayed. Operational failures are not source-insufficiency judgments. Stale revision submissions return 409. Unknown source references and invalid typed edits are rejected. `/api/health` reports provider/model configuration and existing per-file limits, not successful provider access.

## Shared interpretation and optional geometry

`BuildingDescription` remains the shared representation: floors, semantic records, observations, unresolved views and optional geometry. Empty geometric arrays do not make the original evidence unavailable. Sections/elevations can supply source-linked observations and dimensions without becoming floors. Reasoning objects and floor context derive from saved interpretation even when no scene exists.

`extract_interpretation(document, include_geometry=False)` requests source-linked semantics/observations without exhaustive geometry tracing. Each successful result is validated and saved before any generator call. QA can inspect original pages before extraction completes and after reconstruction fails; missing JSON records never establish absent source features.

Explicit generation reuses saved interpretation and requests missing geometry/registration/stair relationships through `enrich_geometry(document) -> DescriptionPatch`. Application validation remains collection-specific and strict. Gemini's wire encodes each complete patch record as a JSON string (or null for removal): the combined typed union was rejected by the endpoint, while generic objects produced empty records. Decoded record objects still pass local typed `DescriptionPatch` validation. OpenAI retains its typed transport. This adaptation does not permit executable code, unknown fields, arbitrary identity changes or invented user provenance. See the verification report for controlled probes and actual live outcomes.

Typed patches preserve existing persistent IDs and require original source evidence. A floor metadata replacement cannot execute implicit nested edits. Its nested copies must preserve base/current ID order and length and exactly match base/current records or separately declared same-floor, same-collection replacements. The floor operation retains staged nested arrays; every separate edit still passes normal source, identity, review and provenance checks. Any invalid operation rejects the entire candidate.

Missing-geometry requests are shared between local detection and both providers. A valid wall segment does not require an optional footprint; already complete geometry is reused. Missing registration applies to non-reference floors only. These requests guide targeted enrichment, not source completeness judgments. Deterministic IFC generation, reopening and original-coordinate overlays support source review. Existing usable geometry is retained on invalid/rejected replacements. A first model can be published as preview while review runs; preview status is not a fidelity guarantee. Concept styling never enters source counts, QA evidence or IFC facts.

## Conversation and reviewed answers

`AskRequest` contains `document_id`, `question` and optional `revision_id`, `request_id`, `conversation_id`, `reply_to`, `clarification_response`. `conversation_id` is the selected building ID. Async repeated `request_id` reuses its question job. History comes from the server's saved building conversation; client-supplied assistant assertions are not accepted as evidence.

Messages carry `id`, `role`, `revision_id`, `timestamp`, optional job/request/reply references, and either user `question` or assistant `answer`. Clarification replies reference an existing assistant clarification in that building. Earlier answers help resolve phrases such as “the upper floor” but remain fallible context, never additional factual sources.

Intent resolution is separate from source sufficiency. A clarification returns:

```json
{"status":"clarification","answer":"Which floor?","clarification":{"message":"Which floor?","suggestions":["Ground floor","Upper floor","Both"],"free_text_allowed":true},"gate":null,"inspection_passes":0}
```

It has no evidence refusal or reviewed factual draft. Ordinary answers retain `answered|insufficient|unclear`, the three-way sufficiency gate, bounded additional inspection and post-draft review. Answers include `answered_revision_id`, `display_revision_id`, validated original-page `evidence` or native `model_evidence`, conservative `highlight_ids`, `support_summary`, review metadata, and `calculation_results` with source-bound inputs/results. Rejected drafts do not become findings. Chat citations work without 3D and open the exact answered source revision; unreliable geometry associations omit highlights.

Door questions distinguish depicted symbols from all installed building doors. A schedule is not universally required for visible leaves/swings/jambs. Ambiguous openings should be identified individually and connecting doors counted once. Gate, draft and review all apply these rules; generated object totals cannot replace original drawing inspection.

For `sources_only` reasoning, nested `user_provided` calibration/registration/stair connection fields are stripped from the serialized interpretation copy and supplied-value records are omitted. Saved data remains unchanged. Permitted `sources_and_user` answers expose relevant inputs separately, cite `user_value_evidence` IDs and receive server-added `user_value_attributions`; original-source questions cannot silently adopt them.

## Editable inputs and provenance

Assumption rows expose `id`, `scope`, `property`, `label`, `value`, `unit`, `provenance`, `reason`, optional `source`, and `editable`. Provenance distinguishes observed information, inferred interpretations, display assumptions, unknowns and user-provided values. Shared floor assumptions are grouped; source observations are retained separately.

The batch payload is:

```json
{"base_revision_id":"...","edits":[{"property":"floor_height","scope":{"floor_id":"..."},"value":3.4,"unit":"m","reason":"Provided by user"}],"supporting_source_ids":[]}
```

Each edit may also cite `source:{page,bbox,source_id?,source_page?}`. Supporting files must already belong to the building. Implemented properties are:

| Property | Value and scope |
|---|---|
| `floor_height` | Finite positive number; floor scope; `m`, `mm`, `cm`, `ft` or `in`. |
| `display_height` | Positive number; floor scope; physical units above or explicit `relative` display units. |
| `calibration` | `{length:number,segment:[[x,y],[x,y]]}` with distinct normalized endpoints, physical unit and a source region on the selected floor's page. |
| `stair_connection` | Selected stair object/floor; `{target_floor_id,target_feature_id?}` referencing another known floor and optionally its stair. |
| `interpretation_correction` | Nonempty text describing a scoped correction; reviewed through a typed data patch. |

Apply validates the full batch before mutation. Inputs retain their IDs, scope, units, source support, submission/base revision and `user_provided` provenance. Observed source heights are not rewritten as user values. Known source calibration/height conflicts, including section observations with uncertain scope, retain both source facts and submitted inputs and return `needs_attention` without replacing the usable revision. Equivalent calibration is compared using original-page aspect and physical unit conversion.

Numeric changes to an existing scene generate/reopen locally, run loss checks and use one existing original-source/actual-geometry review before publication. The reviewer receives user values separately and must distinguish their authority from source observations. Source-only numeric input persistence does not automatically request 3D. Interpretation corrections invoke the bounded typed-patch workflow. Editing/keystrokes make no model calls. Failed/stopped/rejected candidates retain submitted inputs in the persisted job and preserve the prior usable revision.

A supplied vertical height never establishes XY scale. With unknown horizontal calibration, physical height remains attributed in its original unit; vertical presentation uses the disclosed display convention `1 m = 1.2/2.6 relative units`. The scene stays unscaled. This is a display choice, not an inferred building measurement.

## Geometry, formats and portability

Original-page coordinates, building registration/elevation and viewer-only exploded spacing remain separate. Supported shared-page registration can use relative units without asserting metres. Stacked mode retains generated storey elevations; exploded mode adds spacing. Continuous schematic stairs preserve supported footprints/connectivity with assumed vertical geometry identified. Optional wall footprints preserve supported tapered/angled shapes; explicit hosts remain required for openings.

Native floors come from supplied IFC storeys and containment. Cutaway is a percentage clipping control: 0% is the floor reference and 100% the full reference height. All-floor mode uses each storey's own reference; missing heights and uncontained geometry use displayed fallback references. Clipping does not shrink walls or move openings. Camera, floor/mode selection and assumptions controls survive accepted updates where identities remain valid.

SVG and DXF use the existing normalized-image pipeline, with preserved original bytes, vector/layout metadata and coordinate mappings. Declared document units alone do not establish physical building scale. Unsupported rendering features are reported; external resources are not fetched. DWG is unavailable because no validated converter path exists. See `SOURCE_FORMATS.md` for adapter details.

def gemini_wire_schema(schema: dict) -> dict:
    """Adapt Gemini wire grammar while keeping exact local response validation.

    The current endpoint rejects these bounds for our reconstruction schema. Walk
    schema locations, not arbitrary JSON values: keyword-named properties and
    objects inside default/enum remain ordinary data. Numeric bounds rejected by
    the live Gemini endpoint remain enforced by local validation and other wires.
    """
    result = deepcopy(schema)

    def visit(node):
        if not isinstance(node, dict):
            return
        kind = node.get("type")
        if kind == "array" or isinstance(kind, list) and "array" in kind:
            node.pop("maxItems", None)
        if kind in ("number", "integer") or isinstance(kind,list) and any(value in ("number","integer") for value in kind):
            node.pop("minimum", None)
            node.pop("maximum", None)
        for keyword in ("$defs", "definitions", "properties", "patternProperties", "dependentSchemas"):
            for child in node.get(keyword, {}).values():
                visit(child)
        for keyword in ("anyOf", "allOf", "oneOf", "prefixItems"):
            for child in node.get(keyword, []):
                visit(child)
        for keyword in ("items", "additionalProperties", "contains", "not", "if", "then", "else",
                        "propertyNames", "unevaluatedProperties", "unevaluatedItems"):
            visit(node.get(keyword))

# Full-Story Verification

You are a verification orchestrator. Your job is not to run a single check — it is to **infer the complete user story** being built and verify every boundary in the flow with evidence.

Your focus is the **end-to-end story**, not any single layer.

## When This Triggers

- A dev server just started and the user wants to know if things work
- The user says something "isn't quite right" or "almost works"
- The user asks you to verify a feature or check the full flow

## Step 1 — Infer the User Story

Before checking anything, determine **what is being built**:

1. Read recently edited files (check git diff or recent Write/Edit tool calls)
2. Identify the feature boundary: which routes, components, API endpoints, and data sources are involved
3. Scan `package.json` scripts, route structure (`app/` or `pages/`), and environment files (`.env*`)
4. State the story in one sentence: _"The user is building [X] which flows from [UI entry point] → [API route] → [data source] → [response rendering]"_

**Do not skip this step.** Every subsequent check must be anchored to the inferred story.

## Step 2 — Establish Evidence Baseline

Gather the current state across all layers:

| Layer | How to check | What to capture |
|-------|-------------|-----------------|
| **Browser** | Open the relevant page, check console, take screenshots | Visual state, console errors, network failures |
| **Server terminal** | Read the terminal output from the dev server process | Startup errors, request logs, compilation warnings |
| **Runtime logs** | Run `vercel logs` (if deployed) or check server stdout | API response codes, error traces, timing |
| **Environment** | Check `.env.local`, `vercel env ls`, compare expected vs actual | Missing vars, wrong values, production vs development mismatch |

Report what you find at each layer before proceeding. Use this reporting contract:

> **Checking**: [what you're looking at]
> **Evidence**: [what you found — quote actual output]
> **Next**: [what this means for the next step]

## Step 3 — Walk the Data Flow

Trace the feature's data path from trigger to completion:

1. **UI trigger** — What user action initiates the flow? (button click, page load, form submit)
2. **Client → Server** — What request is made? Check the fetch/action call, verify the URL, method, and payload match the API route
3. **API route handler** — Read the route file. Does it handle the method? Does it validate input? Does it call the right service/database?
4. **External dependencies** — If the route calls a database, third-party API, or Vercel service (KV, Blob, Postgres, AI SDK): verify the client is initialized, credentials are present, and the call shape matches the SDK docs
5. **Response → UI** — Does the response format match what the client expects? Is error handling present on both sides?

At each boundary, check for these common breaks:
- **Missing `await`** on async operations
- **Wrong HTTP method** (GET handler but POST fetch)
- **Env var absent** in runtime but present in `.env.local`
- **Import mismatch** (server module imported in client component or vice versa)
- **Type mismatch** between API response and client expectation
- **Missing error boundary** — unhandled rejection crashes the page silently

## Step 4 — Report With Evidence

Summarize findings in a structured report:

```
## Verification Report: [Feature Name]

**Story**: [one-sentence description of the user story]

### Flow Status

The main session's reviewed reliability commits are `f932467` and `3064e21`. They have not been cherry-picked here. The chat UI preserves their additive recovery-event/submitted-value presentation semantics so later integration does not require restoring the old app.js. Each recovery event's own base revision pins its source link; submitted values are not described as applied unless accepted.

## Environment and artifacts

The UI reuses the existing Python virtual environment through an ignored `.venv` symlink. No dependencies changed. Browser checks use `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/tmp/junction-playwright` and Chromium's software WebGL backend. Separate store: `.runtime/chat-ui-verification`; no existing demo store is mutated. ## Small action/result contract

`POST /api/chat/actions` is an additive intent/validation route, not another job runner. Input: `message`, `request_id`, optional `document_id` and interpretation `revision_id`, plus a captured `workspace`. Output echoes request/document/revision identity and returns `status: ready|clarification`, `actions`, a brief non-factual `message`, and optional focused clarification/suggestions. Existing endpoints execute accepted operations; their results and errors update chat/workspace. The root-owned coordination proposal is authoritative for final operation names; the list below states required capabilities, not competing enum spellings. Root will freeze exact enums in `docs/CHAT_UI_CONTRACT.md` before dependent implementation.

Workspace explicitly stores document/building ID, interpretation revision, displayed geometry revision, view mode (`chat|source|model|concept`), selected IDs, focused ID, camera position/up/target, tour ordered IDs/index/running state, navigation highlighting, answer highlighting and assumption visibility. Also retain floor filter, separation, cutaway and source page/region where applicable. Document revision and geometry revision are distinct because a newer source interpretation can retain older usable geometry.

Use a strict discriminated action schema, with deterministic execution in declared order:

- `show_model` (reuse saved scene; existing reconstruction only when needed), `show_source`, `close_workspace`, `set_camera` (top/front/isometric/fit), `select` (validated IDs), `tour` (start/pause/resume/next/previous), `set_visibility` (answer highlights, navigation highlights, assumptions), `set_view` (inspection/concept), `set_floor`, `set_separation`, `set_cutaway`, `set_theme`.
- `question` forwards the original question and pinned context to the existing reviewed QA route; no factual answer is synthesized by the action interpreter.
- `refine` contains a validated existing `RefinementRequest` batch. Preserve exact user value, unit, scope, source support and attribution; route corrections through `interpretation_correction`. A bare request to improve the existing model uses existing reconstruction `mode: refine`.
- `list_saved`, `open_saved`, `attach_sources`, `new_upload`, `download_ifc`, `download_source`, `retry_extraction`, `stop_job`, `refresh`, `inspect_assumptions`, `inspect_inventory`, `set_comparison` cover existing application operations without separate settings/toolbars. File choice/download still uses browser-native controls reached through chat. Ambiguous saved building, floor, source, job or refinement scope requests a focused choice.

Gemini (or the explicitly configured OpenAI adapter) interprets language once using existing structured transport through an additive adapter. The prompt requests intent and reference selectors, never authoritative facts or fabricated IDs. Supply saved semantic labels/IDs/kinds/floors and current workspace context; no screenshot rediscovery or raw source image pass is needed for navigation. Code resolves `focused`, `selection`, named IDs/labels, kinds and floors against the correct saved revision, validating membership, renderability and source evidence. Duplicate labels produce clarification. Do not resolve by list index, nearest region or similarity guessed by the model. Unresolved objects remain available for source inspection and are excluded from mesh selection/tours.

An explicit modeled-window selection means all renderable, reliably associated saved window records in the requested scope, never every window in the real building or drawing. Report renderable/unresolved coverage without claiming extraction completeness. Native IFC source navigation uses the existing pinned record inspector; do not invent blueprint pages. Drawings use the original stored page/region exactly, including existing coarse-region limitations.

When no scene exists, `show_model` may carry a typed deferred selector such as `{kind:"window",floor_id:null}`. This is a pending navigation request, not a resolved identity list or an assertion that windows were reconstructed. Validate selector type and any existing floor scope immediately; once the existing job publishes an accepted usable scene, application code resolves it against that scene and validates renderability. A failed/stopped/no-mesh reconstruction stops dependent selection, camera and tour actions and reports the retained source/model state. Never manufacture IDs in anticipation of generation. A preview can be shown as preview while review continues, but the pending action must state that status rather than call it complete/reviewed.

Execute action batches in order. Each step returns completed, pending or failed; a pending operation suspends its dependent steps, and failure cancels those steps. Already completed harmless navigation is retained and described; do not claim transaction rollback. Validate the full persistent edit batch before submission using the existing atomic workflow. Do not combine unrelated persistent mutations into an implicit transaction. Output chat text is generated from validated action results/labels; the interpreter's prose cannot become an unreviewed factual answer. Clarification may use concise interpreter text but must ask about the genuine unresolved target/scope.

Malformed actions, absent targets, unsupported edits and stale persistent revisions fail before execution. A provider failure is a recoverable operational error, never source insufficiency or silent regex/fixture fallback. Compact chat buttons may emit typed deterministic actions without another model call. Keep existing upload/page/provider limits; one small intent call adds routing latency, not a second factual review.

## State and sequencing invariants

1. On every submit, synchronously pause the tour and capture an immutable snapshot before any await or queued timer can change focused ID. Cancel queued tour movement. Resolve “this window” against that snapshot. Preserve the captured source revision and stored evidence separately from current display state.
2. Apply asynchronous results only to their request/document epoch. A newer scene swap revalidates selection and tour IDs; removed/unresolved targets are explained and never replaced by another object. Stale refinements return 409 and request an explicit resubmission against the refreshed revision. Old source evidence can still open its pinned revision.
3. Keep navigation selection/highlighting separate from answer highlights and assumption display. Source navigation pauses the tour but preserves its IDs/index, camera and model revision. “Back to the model; next window” restores that tour and advances exactly once. Reaching the end reports completion rather than silently cycling.
4. Camera top-down preserves selection. Frame selection from actual world bounds with active floor offsets; close-ups use reliable geometry/host orientation where available. An ambiguous orientation uses a useful oblique fallback labeled as approximate; never claim an inferred exterior side or physical dimension. Manual orbit/pan/zoom continue to work and update captured camera state.
5. Reuse the existing prepared/atomic revision swap. Preserve surviving IDs, camera, modes and independent toggles. Rejected refinement leaves the previous usable scene visible. Pending, preview/unreviewed, reviewed-with-remaining-issues, stopped and failed states remain distinct in chat.
6. Preserve reliability-session `recovery_events`, `submitted_values`, and each event's base-revision source links when integration brings those additions in. Do not drop those fields while reformatting job cards.
7. Navigation, source inspection and compact actions remain usable while factual QA or reconstruction runs. Use per-request state rather than a global busy lock. Serialize persistent mutations through existing job rules; reject stale results without erasing the next message draft or a newer user navigation. Maintain an explicit navigation epoch, incremented by submit, compact navigation or deliberate gesture start, separately from document epoch and interpretation/geometry revisions. Orbit damping/render ticks do not increment it. A response may mutate the workspace only if its captured epoch still owns the pending navigation; otherwise retain its result in chat without moving the view. A pending reconstruction continuation is tied to its request/epoch and cannot override later navigation. Old source links remain usable through their captured revision even after a stale action is discarded.
8. Keep ephemeral navigation/upload/progress turns in a keyed client message ledger and merge persisted server QA turns by request/job/message IDs. `refreshConversation` must not replace the entire ledger and erase navigation or duplicate answers. Restoring ephemeral navigation turns across a full browser restart is not required; persisted building QA remains the existing authoritative history, and the UI must not claim navigation history was saved.

1. Establish the contract and deterministic interaction fixtures before polishing layout. Fixtures inject provider/action responses and are explicitly labeled test data; no production mock switch or fixture answer fallback.
2. Implement additive routing and validation against existing snapshots. Unit-check malformed/unknown references, duplicate-label ambiguity, stale document/geometry contexts, scoped refinement payloads, native IFC source behavior and provider errors.
3. Implement viewer selection framing, top-down and focused-object close-ups using existing meshes/controls. Add explicit snapshots and pauseable tour state. No source/IFC/geometry mutation.
4. Build Chronicle chat presentation and migrate existing upload, polling, answer/citation, operation and failure presentation into chat. Provide keyboard-accessible attachment/action/citation controls, live progress announcements and retained message drafts.
5. Integrate accepted action execution with existing endpoints. Upload shows “Reading your drawings…” until validated interpretation is available; say sources are retained on failure. QA works before 3D. Requested 3D reuses a cached scene or displays existing job progress. Retain pending semantic selection until newly generated geometry is available, then resolve against that actual revision.

The independent plan reviewer must inspect the existing application directly in Chromium and assess the plan against its actual available operations. The independent implementation reviewer directly exercises the delivered application, not merely reads screenshots or test scripts.

Address these observed problems:

“Chat interpretation failed operationally. No action was executed; your saved sources and usable model remain available.”

2. Original blueprints do not open reliably
“Show the original blueprint” should open the supplied drawing without requiring a selected object. Distinguish whole-document navigation from “show this object in its original blueprint.” For multiple drawings, provide discoverable page/source choices and clarify only genuine ambiguity. Preserve exact stored coordinates and revision-pinned evidence.

3. The interface is too sparse and unintuitive
Revise the earlier restriction against visible controls: chat-first does not mean chat-only.

Provide persistent, compact controls for switching between Blueprints and 3D model, navigating supplied pages, and returning to the current selection. These operations should work immediately without a Gemini call. Preserve camera, selection and tour context across view switches.

Keep Chronicle’s actual light/dark themes and avoid sprawling settings panels, but prioritize discoverability over minimalism.

4. Orbiting incorrectly interrupts pending questions
The current controller invalidates a shared navigation epoch on pointer/wheel interaction and then discards the entire pending intent response.

Separate factual-question execution from workspace navigation. Users must be able to orbit, zoom, pan and switch views while a question completes. Preserve the document/revision and “this object” context captured at submission. Prevent stale navigation from unexpectedly moving the camera, without cancelling a valid question or displaying a generic interruption error.

Keep genuine cross-document and stale-mutation protections.

5. Restore visible provenance and direct evidence linkage
The redesign has hidden essential distinctions between source-supported information, interpretations, user-provided values, display assumptions and decorative proposals.

Provide:
- Discoverable assumption markers, a clear legend and a manual toggle.
- A persistent compact evidence summary for the selected object.
- Direct “Show in original” navigation to exact stored evidence.

# Blueprint QA — hackathon instructions

## Scope
Build a local, lean application: upload JPG/PNG/PDF/SVG/DXF or IFC, ask a construction-plan question, inspect evidence and an interactive Three.js model. Current scope includes explicitly depicted floors via building description → deterministic IfcOpenShell generation → derived IFC → viewer. Read docs/RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md and docs/RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md. V3 uses explicit physical walls, wall-hosted openings, indoor/outdoor spaces, schematic stairs/furnishings/fixtures, source-linked unresolved records and actual-IFC source comparison. Room polygons must never imply enclosure. Defer unseen/invented floors, DWG without a validated converter, Blender/cloud rendering, auth, database and multi-agent runtime.

The active product specification is docs/PRODUCT_SPEC.md, with independently reviewed checkpoints in docs/PRODUCT_PLAN.md. It adds local filesystem bundles, background reconstruction reviews, reviewed QA and the existing concept renderer; these are now authorized scope. Keep the configurable reconstruction model default; Hydrogen was not adopted.

Current source-first scope is docs/SOURCE_FIRST_SPEC.md with reviewed docs/SOURCE_FIRST_PLAN.md and implemented docs/SOURCE_FIRST_CONTRACT.md. Upload saves originals and extracts interpretation; 3D is explicit. Related drawing sources share revision-pinned provenance, source-linked chat and attributed batch user inputs. Keep native IFC separate from grouped drawing sources until mixed evidence validation exists. Read docs/SOURCE_FIRST_VERIFICATION.md for actual live results and remaining fidelity gaps. Focused commits are authorized; do not push.

## Workflow
- Before introducing self-imposed constraints, explicitly communicate what they restrict, why they are needed, whether they are an external requirement or our design choice, and how they might block valid inputs or the demo. Prefer the smallest justified set for this hackathon. Do not silently introduce arbitrary caps or turn this into a blanket approval bureaucracy.
- Read docs/PLAN.md, docs/CONTRACT.md and docs/HANDOFF.md before changing behavior.
- Setup: `bash scripts/bootstrap.sh`. Run: `bash scripts/dev.sh`. Check: `bash scripts/test.sh`. Diagnose: `.venv/bin/python scripts/doctor.py`. Make targets are optional aliases when make is installed.
- Python 3.12+, FastAPI, plain HTML/CSS/JS, server-side Gemini (final demo) or explicit temporary OpenAI adapter. `AI_PROVIDER=gemini|openai`; default Gemini, never auto-failover. One process; no frontend build tool.
- Dependencies live in requirements.in; requirements.txt is the reproducible resolved lock. Coordinate dependency changes with the orchestrator.
- Use `.venv/bin/python`; do not modify system Python. Local sandbox may fail with bwrap: use approved escalated calls if required.
- Never print or commit `.env*` secrets, uploads, provider request bodies, or dataset answers. `.env.example` contains placeholders only.
- Use injected fake providers for deterministic tests. Never present fixture answers as real inference. API failures are operational errors, not evidence-insufficiency judgments.

## Product invariants
- Remain building-type agnostic: preserve original space labels and meaningful non-residential features. Unknown use gets neutral concept styling and explicit schematic fallbacks, never automatic residential furnishing. Separate floor plans from sections, elevations and site plans; unsupported views/features remain source-linked unresolved records without invented floors. Detailed domes/roofs are out of scope.
- Concept styling/proposals never enter reasoning evidence, source counts or IFC exports. Inspection/concept use the same saved revision. Original sources and usable revisions survive operational failure, stop and restart.
- One overall source-sufficiency gate: sufficient / insufficient / unclear. Inspect original source material, not only a model summary.
- Allow derivations with supported inputs. No invented dimensions as facts; no model confidence advertised as accuracy.
- Unclear gets at most one targeted additional inspection; unresolved stays unclear.
- Drawing answers cite normalized page/region evidence; IFC answers cite inspected GlobalId/property records. Unknown source references fail validation. Unreliable object mappings retain source evidence without highlighting.
- Genuine source IFC counts use the complete semantic catalog, including geometry-less objects. Generated IFC is always drawing-derived, including after reopening: restore original pages, inferred status and assumptions; never run native factual IFC shortcuts on it. Unknown scale uses an explicit context-dependent display unit, not measured metres. Supported calibration does not make assumed heights or generated geometry factual evidence.
- Missing information is scoped to inspected material. Similar-building ideas/defaults are explicitly proposals; never factual evidence about this building.
- Ground-truth questions.jsonl is evaluation-only, never runtime context.
- Gate sufficiency does not establish answer correctness. Check references and calculations; test confident failures too.

## Collaboration
The root agent is the orchestrator and owns architecture, contracts, environment and integration. Delegate bounded tasks to a planner, an independent plan reviewer, backend/frontend implementers, and an independent implementation reviewer. Reviewers must not review their own implementation as the independent review.

1. **Plan:** The planner proposes the smallest hackathon-sized implementation, explicit exclusions, file ownership, dependencies and testable acceptance criteria.
2. **Plan review loop:** The plan reviewer identifies blocking gaps, unnecessary scope and missing checks. The planner revises the plan and responds to each finding; the reviewer checks the revision. Allow at most two review rounds, then the orchestrator resolves remaining disagreements using evidence or scope reduction. Begin dependent implementation only after planning blockers are resolved. Do not reopen settled scope without new evidence or a user-requested change.
3. **Implementation:** Assign backend/frontend work with clear file ownership and a shared contract. Implementers edit only assigned paths, communicate contract changes first, and do not revert another agent's changes. Parallelize independent tasks; coordinate dependencies through the orchestrator.
4. **Implementation review loop:** A read-only reviewer reports actionable findings with file locations, reproduction evidence where possible, and whether each finding blocks acceptance. Route findings to the responsible implementer, apply fixes, run relevant checks, and re-review the affected behavior. Repeat for unresolved blockers; keep optional improvements deferred unless needed for the agreed scope. If a blocker cannot be resolved, report it explicitly rather than declaring completion.
5. **Integration and completion:** The orchestrator verifies the integrated user flow against the acceptance criteria. Stop when those criteria are met, required checks pass, and no blocking findings remain. Agent agreement alone is not evidence of correctness. Record unresolved limitations and verification gaps in the handoff.

Keep review rounds focused on changed behavior and outstanding findings. No commits, pushes or deployment unless requested.

## Definition of done
Working image/PDF upload and source preview, question/answer flow, explicit insufficient/unclear states, visible citations, bounded provider calls, credential-safe errors, useful tests, documented setup and limitations. Live provider claims require a successful live run; otherwise clearly report unverified integration.

# Chat actions and workspace contract

UI branch `feat/chat-first-ui`, worktree `/tmp/junction-chat-ui`, base `fdfd4e3`. Coordination lives at `/tmp/junction-ui-coordination.md`. This additive boundary never replaces extraction, QA, refinement, persistence or reconstruction. Main session owns those pipelines.

## Request and result

`POST /api/chat/actions` takes `{message,request_id,document_id:null|string,revision_id:null|string,workspace:{geometry_revision_id:null|string,view_mode:"chat|source|model|concept",selected_ids:[],focused_id:null|string,camera:null|object,tour:{ids:[],index:-1,running:false},navigation_epoch:0,highlighting:true,answer_highlighting:true,show_assumptions:false,floor_id:null|string,exploded:false,cutaway:100}}`.

Capture and deep-copy workspace synchronously at submit; pause timer before awaiting. A request does not accept client object names, source boxes or screenshots as evidence. `revision_id` means current interpretation; `geometry_revision_id` means displayed saved geometry. Camera uses viewer `getCameraState()`; damping is not a navigation epoch change. User submissions, compact navigation and manual viewer interaction invalidate older navigation responses. Polls and expected reconstruction swaps do not falsely invalidate their pending action.

Response echoes `request_id,document_id,revision_id,geometry_revision_id,navigation_epoch` and adds `{status:"ready|clarification",actions:[],message,clarification:null|{message,suggestions:[]},usage:{}}`. Message is a deterministic operation summary; factual output only comes from reviewed QA. Clarification concerns intent, never the evidence-sufficiency gate. Operational errors retain existing safe HTTP detail format; 409 means stale context. One selected-provider structured call, existing timeout/output budget, no retry/fallback. Known compact actions execute locally without interpretation.

Provider transport uses `WireChatIntent`: one action-type enum with nullable typed fields. Null fields are removed before strict operation-specific validation; unrelated non-null fields fail rather than being silently discarded. This avoids the broad-union branch ambiguity observed in live Gemini source navigation without changing the public action contract or provider implementation.

## Typed actions

Every action has a literal `type`. Optional keys below default to null/empty. Unknown types/keys and invalid references fail validation.

| Type | Fields / behavior |
|---|---|
| `show_model` | Reuse cached scene or await existing reconstruction; preserve active tour. |
| `select` | `selector:{target:"focused|selection|all|named",kind:null|string,label:null|string,floor:null|string,ids:[]}`, server outputs `ids`, `unresolved_ids`, `deferred` (bool). Empty scene permits only semantic deferred selector; resolve after actual geometry arrives. No fabricated IDs. |
| `show_source` | Same optional `selector`; output `object_id`, `source`, `source_revision_id` from saved revision. Optional explicit `page` for whole original page. Focused references use captured geometry revision. Native source opens record inspector. |
| `close_workspace` | Retain model/camera/tour paused. |
| `set_camera` | `preset:"top|fit|isometric"`; preserve selections. |
| `tour` | `command:"start|pause|resume|next|previous"`; start uses navigation selected IDs, excludes unrenderable records. End stops without cycling. |
| `set_visibility` | `target:"answer_highlights|navigation_highlights|assumptions"`, `enabled:boolean`. Independent state. |
| `set_view` | `mode:"model|concept|source"`. |
| `set_floor` | `floor_id` resolved server-side, null means all; model may propose `label`. |
| `set_separation` | `enabled:boolean`. |
| `set_cutaway` | `percent:number` in existing 0–100 domain. |
| `set_theme` | `theme:"light|dark|system"`. Exact Chronicle tokens. |
| `question` | `question:string`, `revision_id`, `navigation_reference:null|{object_id,source,source_revision_id}`; original message preserved. For a focused question append deterministic clearly labeled navigation reference to existing question text and pin its source revision. Do not introduce an AskRequest field or model-authored factual paraphrase. Respect its existing text length bound. |
| `refine` | `edits` is existing UserEdit batch, `supporting_source_ids:[]`; server validates with existing prepare_inputs without publication. Final execution sends existing RefinementRequest with current captured base. |
| `reconstruct` | `mode:"refine|reconstruct"`; reuse existing job route. |
| `list_saved` | Show saved choices in chat. |
| `open_saved` | `building_id` validated against saved catalog; model may propose `label`. |
| `attach_sources` / `new_upload` | Native file chooser from compact chat control. Existing upload/append routes. |
| `download_ifc` | Existing saved artifact URL; derived provenance unchanged. |
| `download_source` | `source_id` validated; ambiguity asks which source. |
| `retry_extraction` / `refresh` | Existing endpoints. |
| `stop_job` | `job_id` validated against selected building; ambiguity asks which job. |
| `inspect_assumptions` / `inspect_inventory` | Source-linked rows in chat, not a settings panel; no mesh for unresolved records. |
| `set_comparison` | `enabled:boolean`, optional `layer:"spaces|walls|openings|features|unresolved"`, optional `opacity` in the existing 10–90 percent control range; uses the existing actual-IFC source overlay. |
| `help` | Compact examples and available operations in chat. |

Model selectors resolve exact saved IDs/labels/kinds/floors in code. Duplicate labels clarify. Saved modeled-window selection reports coverage as modeled records, not all real/source windows. Source boxes are copied unchanged; never synthesized tighter boxes. Focused removed objects retain old source evidence, but persistent edits must target current surviving identities. No nearest-object or list-index substitution.

Persistent numeric edits must be explicitly attributed to an adjacent quantity/unit pair in the submitted message (digits and common English number words are supported). Calibration requires explicit normalized original-page endpoints; the navigation catalog cannot establish them. Unsupported phrasing clarifies. Any supplied edit source must exactly match a scoped saved source region. Existing attributed-input validation and review remain the final mutation authority.

Execute actions in order, stopping dependent actions on failure. A deferred selector waits for the explicitly requested reconstruction, then resolves using actual new scene records and checks the request/document/navigation epoch. Partial preview and failed review are reported honestly; no automatic extra reconstruction loop. Revision replacements use existing atomic viewer swap; revalidate tour IDs and pause/report lost targets. Source mode retains ordered IDs/index and model camera so back/next advances exactly once.

## Viewer interface

`getCameraState()` / `setCameraState(snapshot)`; `frameIds(ids,{topDown:false}) -> {framed_ids,unavailable_ids}`; `focusObject(id) -> {focused_id,orientation:"geometry|uncertain|unavailable",note}`; `setTheme("light|dark")`. Existing select, setHighlights, setHighlightsEnabled, setShowAssumptions, setFloorFilter, setExploded, setMode and cutaway methods remain. Geometry covariance can establish a window axis; it does not establish exterior side. Ambiguous axes use a labeled approximate oblique camera. Z-up orbit remains; top-down respects the existing numerical polar epsilon.

## Presentation and compatibility

Navigation turns/progress are ephemeral UI records retained across server conversation refresh, separate from persisted factual conversation. Answers are rendered once with citations and expandable existing checks. Saved building/job state remains backend-owned. Recovery events and submitted values are not evidence of publication: preserve labels and event.base_revision_id source pins. Failed/stopped/needs_attention outcomes retain usable models and original sources.

Chronicle tokens originate at `https://github.com/Programmercloud-cmd/AI_Chronicle_UI/blob/main/src/web/styles/global.css`, blob `4396f7a3594369ea3a38c6c0ebdb620496f9703c`: light background/surface/text/muted/line/accent/focus `#fbfaf8/#ffffff/#241f1a/#716a62/#ded9d2/#b95318/#1769aa`; dark `#121110/#191816/#eeeae4/#aaa39a/#403c37/#ef8a4c/#75bfff`.

Verification must distinguish explicit deterministic fixtures, actual imported artifacts/backend responses, and new live-provider runs. No fixture fallback in production. Full matrix in CHAT_UI_PLAN.md.

Main reliability session agreed the additive routing and ownership on 2026-11-14 in the coordination record. All request/action IDs and finite camera/control values are validated against saved revisions; providers close in finally. Mutation actions use their captured base without silently rebasing subsequent edits. Main-owned recovery fields retain event-specific source revisions and submitted-versus-accepted attribution.
# Chat-first UI — verification and handoff

Implemented in `/tmp/junction-chat-ui`, branch `feat/chat-first-ui`, from `fdfd4e3`. Plan, backend, viewer and integrated UI passed independent review, including direct Chromium interaction. No push or modification of another worktree. Reconstruction, refinement, QA, persistence and provider implementations remain owned by the main session.

## Delivery

[CHAT_UI_PLAN.md](CHAT_UI_PLAN.md) records the reviewed plan; [CHAT_UI_CONTRACT.md](CHAT_UI_CONTRACT.md) defines captured workspace, typed actions, identity resolution and existing-operation adapters. Main-session agreement and integration replies are in `/tmp/junction-ui-coordination.md`.

Initial presentation is chat with attachments. Visual requests open a right workspace. Chat covers saved buildings, upload/append, source/model/concept views, selection, cameras, tours, independent visibility, floors, cutaway, separation, comparison, assumptions/inventory, downloads, retries, reconstruction/refinement and job stopping. Existing app.js operations retain hidden compatibility DOM anchors; they are not exposed toolbars. Answers render once with citations/checks. Exact Chronicle light/dark tokens come from `AI_Chronicle_UI/src/web/styles/global.css`, blob `4396f7a3594369ea3a38c6c0ebdb620496f9703c`.

Submission synchronously pauses the tour and copies focus, ordered IDs, position, camera and revision. Code resolves identities; no screenshot rediscovery. Eight-window selection, top-down, tour/captured interruption, pinned original evidence, same-tour next, assumptions/highlights, failures, unresolved source-only records, orbit/zoom/pan, floor/cutaway/separation and native property records passed without JavaScript errors or phantom native drawing pages. Evidence: `/tmp/chat-ui-artifact-check.json`.

## New live Gemini evidence

Configured Gemini and the existing reviewed QA pipeline were used; no production fixture/fallback. Final live Chromium sequence on saved11397 passed:

| Message | Result | Intent latency |
|---|---|---:|
| Show me all windows in the 3D model. | Cached model; 8 rendered IDs, 2 separately unresolved. | 14.69 s |

## Choices and limitations

- Natural-language navigation makes one intent call (about 8–22 s measured). Compact controls and manual orbit/zoom/pan are deterministic and avoid that call. Tour pause/capture occurs immediately.
- One extra factual intent failed operationally and succeeded on later explicit verification calls with unchanged code; the original cause was not captured. General intent reliability remains a limitation, not a claim established by the successful sequences.
- Tour timing is five seconds, with pause/next/resume; no object cap was added.
- Actual mesh covariance guides close-ups. Minor/major horizontal variance below 0.16 permits a geometry-aligned view; ambiguous axes get a labeled approximate oblique view. This never changes geometry or establishes exterior orientation. Z-up top-down retains the orbit controller's numerical epsilon.
- Persistent numeric edits require an explicit quantity/unit pair; digits/common English number words are supported. Unrecognized phrasing clarifies. Calibration currently requires normalized original-page endpoints plus distance: the navigation catalog has no authoritative distance endpoints to invent. Model-authored boxes cannot replace exact scoped saved source regions.
- Fresh live extraction/reconstruction and live refinement-quality assessment were not repeated here; those are the main session's work. Existing source-fidelity limitations remain. OpenAI transport is deterministically tested, not newly live-verified.
- Navigation/progress turns are session UI state. Existing factual conversation/building/job persistence remains backend-owned.
- Legacy browser tests tied to removed toolbars remain opt-in; the new suites cover changed interactions, and the full default suite passes.

## Run and integrate

```

Preserve both sets on integration: the chat renderer understands recovery events, event-specific base revisions/evidence and submitted-versus-applied attribution.

This is a **local UI** delivery. The main session's later public-access/deployment work is separately owned. No unlock UI, visitor isolation or shared-example copy contract was invented here. HTTP401 is displayed as an operational error and never silently retried. Public catalog scoping and mutation authorization must be enforced by deployment integration, not assumed from chat selectors.
# Public demo access plan

Status: independently approved after restoring authenticated QA on pinned examples. The access module and 54 focused tests are implemented; root route/UI integration and independent browser verification remain required. Work on `blueprint-qa-isolated`; no push. This plan covers public browsing of nine curated examples and shared-code access to paid/private work. Deployment is separately owned. No database, per-user accounts, new inference limits or architectural subsystem.

## Confirmed behavior and risks

`app/main.py` currently exposes every building, current scene, original source, conversation and job without access checks. Upload, extraction, reconstruction, refinement and both QA endpoints can invoke providers or mutate stored state. The newly integrated chat/action routes must receive the same protection, including paths that invoke tools indirectly.

`BuildingStore` has no fork/clone operation. `add()` uses original-byte SHA256 as the building ID; reuploading a curated source selects its shared building rather than creating a private copy. `add_many()` may append sources and `_alias()` can update shared source metadata. Merely blocking example reconstruction URLs is insufficient. `prepare()` creates another revision of the same building, not a workspace. `commit()` rewrites scene building/revision URLs; blindly copying a directory or exporting/reimporting its derived IFC is not a proven independent copy operation.

Existing QA appends operational job/conversation records and answers from a document snapshot; it does not commit source, interpretation, geometry or user-input revisions. Authenticated QA on curated examples is therefore allowed without a workspace copy. These conversations/jobs remain private to all shared-code holders. Public unversioned scene/page/export endpoints currently follow CURRENT. A building-only allowlist would therefore expose a later unreviewed revision. Building detail also includes jobs; conversation/job responses can contain private prompts, inputs and diagnostics. Resource storage is shared across buildings, so knowing a source hash must never grant public access.

## Smallest server control

Add `app/public_access.py` plus dedicated tests; root integrates its helpers into `app/main.py` and the new chat routes. Keep local development unchanged when explicit public-demo mode is disabled. In public mode, missing/invalid access configuration or manifest fails closed at startup, not open to all data.

Suggested configuration:

- `BLUEPRINT_PUBLIC_DEMO=1` explicitly enables the controls.
- `BLUEPRINT_PUBLIC_EXAMPLES_FILE` points to a deployment-local JSON manifest of curated `{building_id, revision_id, title}` records. The selected nine entries are content choices, not a new general application limit. Validate unique IDs, exact existing immutable revisions and their sources when opening the server. Do not scan all storage and auto-publish it.
- `BLUEPRINT_DEMO_ACCESS_CODE_HASH` contains a salted stdlib scrypt verifier produced locally from hidden terminal input. Never request the code in chat, put it in command arguments, commit it, or include it in logs. A small local administrative setup command can print only a deployment-file location, not the credential.
- `BLUEPRINT_DEMO_SESSION_SECRET` is a random server secret supplied through the protected deployment environment. Rotate it to invalidate shared-code sessions. Deployment owns secure provisioning and HTTPS.

Use a signed host-only session cookie (`HttpOnly`, `Secure` in public HTTPS mode, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/`, no Domain). The browser-session cookie avoids introducing an arbitrary session-duration cap for this hackathon. The signature binds the editor scope and a random nonce; include verifier version/digest in signing context so changing the access code invalidates existing sessions. Do not store the code itself in cookies, localStorage or JavaScript. Shared-code holders intentionally share the privileged workspace; this is not per-user isolation.

Suggested module interfaces, subject to root approval:

- `PublicAccess.from_environment()` validates mode/configuration and loads exact example IDs/revisions.
- `access.is_editor(request)` verifies the cookie without reading request-body secrets into logs.
- `access.require_editor(request)` rejects unauthorized paid/mutating calls before body processing/provider construction where possible.
- `access.document(store, request, building_id, revision_id=None)` resolves a public example to its pinned revision, rejects other revision IDs and private IDs uniformly, and permits code holders to read private work. Curated example reads remain pinned for both audiences.
- `access.require_editable(request, building_id)` rejects source/model/interpretation mutations of shared examples even for editors. It does not prohibit code-gated QA or stopping its operational jobs. `access.question_document(...)` forces exact manifest-revision snapshots for example QA and rejects a conflicting supplied revision; private work retains existing revision checks.
- `access.public_buildings(store)` returns only curated pinned public descriptors, without jobs/history/conversation. Root keeps code-holder private lists separate or filters appropriately for the chosen view.
- A default-deny API middleware guards every non-read request and rejects public reads outside the exact listed routes. Root invokes editable/document helpers for identity-bearing requests after validated parsing. Neither UI-hidden buttons nor possession of an ID authorize an operation.

Add `GET /api/access` returning only `{public_demo, can_work}`; `POST /api/access/unlock` accepts the code in a JSON body and returns an empty success with cookie; `POST /api/access/lock` removes the cookie. Unlock necessarily accepts a missing session; it invokes no inference. Do not reveal whether a private building/job exists in unauthorized responses. Restrict browser state-changing requests to same-origin using Origin/Fetch-Metadata checks in addition to SameSite; keep explicitly configured local test clients working without weakening deployed cross-origin rejection. No permissive CORS.

## Route policy and pinned content

| Existing/new surface | Public visitor | Shared-code holder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/`, `/chat`, `/static/*`, minimal health/access status | Public application assets/status | Same |
| `GET /api/buildings` | Nine manifest-selected pinned examples only | Private work plus curated entries, clearly distinguished |
| Example building detail / assumptions | Pinned approved revision; no jobs, history or conversation | Same public snapshot for curated ID; private workspace detail permitted |
| Document page / scene / `model.ifc` | Resolve allowlisted building to pinned revision | Same pinned example or selected private workspace |
| Revision page / native IFC evidence | Exact manifest building+revision pair only | Other revisions only for private work |
| Original-source download / arbitrary source resource | Not public | Only validated membership in accessible private workspace or explicitly authenticated example source access |
| Conversation and QA job detail | Not public, including examples | Shared privileged history, including example QA; never included in anonymous building responses |
| Internal diagnostics/history artifact paths | Not public | No new raw diagnostic-serving endpoint |
| Upload/source append, extraction, reconstruction, legacy POST scene, refinement | Requires code; no provider call before authorization | Private work only; shared example source/model revisions remain immutable |
| Both QA routes and QA chat actions | Requires code | Allowed on exact pinned examples and private work; only operational history/jobs are appended |
| Chat/actions that modify source/model/inputs | Requires code | Same immutable-model guard as direct mutation endpoints, applied before action execution |
| Stop QA job | Requires code | Allowed for private or example QA jobs; never grants reconstruction/mutation authority |
| Unrecognized API path/method | Deny | Normal routed behavior after editor check; future paid APIs inherit protection |

For example export, the existing derived IFC embeds original pages, source files, assumptions and user-value provenance. Manifest curation therefore approves those embedded artifacts too; hiding a raw-source URL does not make data inside an approved export private. Inspect selected artifacts for unrelated uploads, user messages or private filenames before listing them. Do not redact geometry provenance or silently strip original-source evidence to claim privacy.

Any new public route needs an explicit policy entry. OpenAPI/docs may remain editor-only; they are not needed for public browsing. Public health should not include storage contents, secrets or exception values. All sensitive responses and access responses use no-store. No uploaded storage path is mounted as static content.

## Immutable examples without workspace copies

Define immutability narrowly: the curated example's sources, interpretation, supplied geometric values and model revisions cannot change through the demo. Authenticated users may ask new questions against its exact pinned originals. The existing question flow appends private operational conversation and job records; those are allowed and visible only to shared-code holders. A QA answer or clarification must never trigger refinement or persist user-provided dimensions as source facts. Model-changing chat actions call the same immutable guard as the direct API.

No clone operation is needed for this milestone. Geometry/source edit attempts return a precise `409`: “This shared example model is read-only. Upload another blueprint to edit.” Do not suggest a nonexistent copy action or block paid QA behind a copy requirement. Shared-code holders intentionally share these conversations and private uploads; disclose that there is no account isolation.

Guard all uploaded multipart parts before invoking `add_many`, `_resource`, `_alias` or extraction. A curated source at any position may select or alias the existing resource; a multipart group beginning with it can otherwise append private sources to the public bundle. Code holders may select the existing read-only example or receive the explicit immutable result, but the request cannot mutate shared source metadata, trigger extraction, or create a misleading editable duplicate. A distinct private original remains uploadable.

Pin example QA at the snapshot boundary, not only by overwriting the request's revision string: `JobRunner.question()` currently loads CURRENT and rejects mismatches, and `_question()` rechecks highlights against CURRENT. Root must pass/resolve the exact manifest revision for both source inference and displayed model/highlight comparison. The synchronous `/api/ask` and new chat dispatch use the same pinned document helper. Source citations and answer revision IDs continue pointing to the original pinned revision even if CURRENT differs. A client-supplied conflicting revision must fail rather than select hidden data. Read-only source QA remains operationally separate from immutable model edits.

The existing store lacks a safe clone primitive: new independent bundle identity, metadata creation and portable IFC lineage require additional testing. Defer all copy UI/API/store work. Keep source hashes/object IDs/coordinates/assumptions untouched for public examples and existing private work.

## Ownership and integration
